## PR Checklist

## What is the current behavior?

The `withErrorBoundaries()` JSDoc lists event handlers among the errors caught by the router outlet. As confirmed in the issue, event-handler errors are outside rendering and are not handled by these boundaries.

Issue Number: Fixes #72162

## What is the new behavior?

Remove event handlers from that list. This changes only the API documentation; runtime behavior is unchanged.

- Runtime tests and the full Angular build/lint suite were not run for this comment-only edit.

Thanks to @Dev199092 for the report and @JeanMeche for [clarifying the intended behavior](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/72162#issuecomment-7084534983).

Issues.Title: Service worker caches `Cache-Control: no-store` responses for asset group `urls` and serves them to the next user after logout
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

service-worker

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description


For URLs matched by an asset group's `urls`, `handleFetch()` answers from CacheStorage whenever it has a copy:

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/53ef99a543e037b64c596e9c3e147cb365062cea/packages/service-worker/worker/src/assets.ts#L141-L164

and `fetchAndCacheOnce()` keys in-flight requests by URL only, then stores the response without looking at `Cache-Control`:

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/53ef99a543e037b64c596e9c3e147cb365062cea/packages/service-worker/worker/src/assets.ts#L300-L336

So:

- A response sent with `Cache-Control: no-store` is stored and served to later requests for that URL, whatever their credentials. On a shared browser, the next user gets the previous user's response. The [docs](https://angular.dev/ecosystem/service-workers/config) say `urls` resources "are cached according to their HTTP headers", and `no-store` means a cache [must not store the response](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111#section-5.2.2.5).
- A request that arrives while another request for the same URL is in flight gets that request's response, even if one was sent with the user's cookie and the other with `credentials: 'omit'`.

Minimal example:

```json
{ "name": "api", "installMode": "lazy", "resources": { "urls": ["/api/**"] } }
```

```ts
await firstValueFrom(http.post('/auth/login', { user: 'alice' }));
await firstValueFrom(http.get('/api/me'));

await firstValueFrom(http.post('/auth/logout', null));
await firstValueFrom(http.get('/api/me', { credentials: 'omit', cache: 'no-store' }));

await firstValueFrom(http.post('/auth/login', { user: 'bob' }));
await firstValueFrom(http.get('/api/me'));
```

`/api/me` is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store, private` and `Vary: Cookie`, and returns `{"user":null}` without a session. The last two requests both get alice's response:

```json
{ "user": "alice", "email": "alice@example.test", "request": 1 }
```

Bob's request has no options, so the request's `credentials` and `cache` don't matter here. `Vary: Cookie` doesn't help either: asset groups always match with `ignoreVary: true`, and requests in the worker don't carry the `Cookie` header.

The requests above:

| Request                                                                | Service worker bypassed | Service worker active |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------- |
| `GET /api/me` as alice                                                 | alice, request 1        | alice, request 1      |
| `GET /api/me` after logout, `credentials: 'omit'`, `cache: 'no-store'` | `null`, request 2       | alice, request 1      |
| `GET /api/me` as bob                                                   | bob, request 3          | alice, request 1      |

Then, as alice, a URL that isn't cached yet, and 50 ms later the same URL with `credentials: 'omit'`:

| Request                                     | Service worker bypassed | Service worker active |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------- |
| `GET /api/me?race=…`                        | alice, request 4        | alice, request 2      |
| `GET /api/me?race=…`, `credentials: 'omit'` | `null`, request 5       | alice, request 2      |

Both cases use the setup of GHSA-95qp-cmmw-mgqv (precondition 2), but neither is the request rebuilding fixed in #68904. That request now keeps `credentials: 'omit'` and `cache`, and the server never gets a cookie for those requests: in both cases the worker answers without sending them. The advisory also notes that CacheStorage is governed by `ngsw-config.json` and `ngsw-bypass`, not `Request.cache`. The first case is about the response's own `Cache-Control`, which the docs say `urls` follow, and the second one doesn't come from CacheStorage.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

See https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/ng-service-worker-cache-bypass

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular CLI       : 22.3.0
Angular           : 22.3.0
Node.js           : 24.16.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.13.0
Operating System  : win32 x64

┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│ Package                   │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │
├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤
│ @angular/build            │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/cli              │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/common           │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/compiler         │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/compiler-cli     │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/core             │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ @angular/service-worker   │ 22.3.0            │ 22.3.0            │
│ rxjs                      │ 7.8.2             │ ~7.8.0            │
│ typescript                │ 6.0.3             │ ~6.0.2            │
└───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘
```

### Anything else?

I think we can consider this a bypass of https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-95qp-cmmw-mgqv

Issues.Title: router: `withErrorBoundaries` docs say event handler errors are caught, but an error thrown in a `(click)` handler does not render the route's `errorComponent`
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

router

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

The JSDoc of `withErrorBoundaries()` says:

> errors thrown within routed components (lifecycle hooks, template bindings, resource loaders, and event handlers) are caught by the RouterOutlet

In my app, an error thrown from a `(click)` handler of a routed component is not caught: the route's `errorComponent` is not rendered, `onError` is not called, the component stays on screen, and the error only goes to the global `ErrorHandler` (browser console).

Errors thrown in the constructor are handled as documented (the `errorComponent` is rendered).

```ts
{ path: 'ctor',  component: CtorPage,  errorComponent: ErrorFallback },  // constructor throws -> fallback rendered
{ path: 'click', component: ClickPage, errorComponent: ErrorFallback },  // (click) handler throws -> fallback NOT rendered
```

Expected: either the `errorComponent` is rendered for the click handler error, or the documentation does not list event handlers. I cannot tell which of the two you intend, so I am reporting the mismatch.

Also not caught in my tests: an error in a child component's `output()` handler, and in a host `(click)` listener. Same result in a production build.

From reading the code, listener errors seem to go through `executeListenerWithErrorHandling` in `@angular/core`, which calls `handleUncaughtError`, and not through the boundary lookup used for other errors. That is only my reading of the source; I did not debug it further.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/Dev199092/error-boundary-event-handler-repro

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
ERROR Error: save failed
    at ClickPage.go (...)

(only in the browser console; the page does not change)
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular CLI       : 22.3.0
Angular           : 22.3.0
Node.js           : 24.20.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64

Package                   Installed Version
@angular/build            22.3.0
@angular/cli              22.3.0
@angular/common           22.3.0
@angular/compiler         22.3.0
@angular/compiler-cli     22.3.0
@angular/core             22.3.0
@angular/forms            22.3.0
@angular/platform-browser 22.3.0
@angular/router           22.3.0
typescript                6.0.3
```

### Anything else?

Workaround that I verified: catch the error in the handler, store it in a signal, and rethrow it from a template binding. Then the boundary renders the `errorComponent`.

Not tested: zone.js apps, other browsers, SSR.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "router: `withErrorBoundaries` docs say event handler errors are caught, but an error thrown in a `(click)` handler does not render the route's `errorComponent`" (#72162)

Issues.Title: compiler: `ngNonBindable` on the root element of an `@empty` block crashes the template compiler ("All attributes should have an element-like target", no file or line)
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler ### Is this a regression? No ### Description An element with `ngNonBindable` that is the root element of an `@empty` block makes the template compiler fail with an internal error. The message names no file, line, component or template, so in a larger project it is very hard to find the cause. ```html @for (item of items; track item) {

{{ item }}

} @empty {

No items {{ not interpolated }}

} ``` Expected: the template compiles, and the paragraph shows the curly braces as plain text. Actual: `ng build` fails with `Angular compilation emit failed` and `Error: All attributes should have an element-like target.` With `ng serve` already running, the page keeps its old content and the browser shows an error overlay ("Angular compilation initialization failed"). If the first build fails, `ng serve` does not start at all. It only fails when the element is the (single) root element of the `@empty` block. Any tag fails (`div`, `span`, `p`, `input`, `svg`). It works: - when the element is wrapped in ``, `` or another element inside `@empty`; - when `@empty` has two root elements; - when `ngNonBindable` is on a child element; - in `@if`, `@else`, `@switch` and `@defer` blocks and in the `@for` body. I found it with a template fuzzer (3 of 200 random templates crashed) and minimised one of them. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug https://github.com/Dev199092/empty-nonbindable-repro ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true ✘ [ERROR] Angular compilation emit failed. [plugin angular-compiler] Error: All attributes should have an element-like target. at lookupElement$2 (node_modules/@angular/compiler/fesm2022/compiler.mjs:9027:11) at Object.specializeBindings [as fn] (node_modules/@angular/compiler/fesm2022/compiler.mjs:9050:28) at transform (node_modules/@angular/compiler/fesm2022/compiler.mjs:19316:13) at compileComponentFromMetadata (node_modules/@angular/compiler/fesm2022/compiler.mjs:22653:3) at ComponentDecoratorHandler.compileFull (node_modules/@angular/compiler-cli/bundles/chunk-IRDAAWGT.js:13386:17) ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular CLI : 22.3.0 Angular : 22.3.0 Node.js : 24.20.0 Package Manager : npm 11.19.0 Operating System : darwin arm64 Package Installed Version @angular/build 22.3.0 @angular/cli 22.3.0 @angular/common 22.3.0 @angular/compiler 22.3.0 @angular/compiler-cli 22.3.0 @angular/core 22.3.0 typescript 6.0.3 ``` ### Anything else? Workaround: wrap the element in `` (one line), or put `ngNonBindable` on a child element, or use `@if (items.length === 0)` instead of `@empty`. I did not test older Angular versions, and I do not know the cause. It looks like the attribute handling for the root element of an `@empty` block, but that is only a guess.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "compiler: `ngNonBindable` on the root element of an `@empty` block crashes the template compiler ("All attributes should have an element-like target", no file or line)" (#72161)

Issues.Title: fix(forms): clear number inputs when the model value is infinite
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #72157

When a `[formField]` bound to a number-like input (number, range, datetime-local, or date-type inputs with a numeric model) gets `Infinity` or `-Infinity` from the model, `setNativeNumberControlValue` writes it to `valueAsNumber`, which throws. The input keeps its old value and the rest of the view update is skipped.

## What is the new behavior?

Non-finite values are handled like `NaN`: the input is cleared and nothing throws.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: fix(forms): clear native number inputs for infinite signal form values
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

When a Signal Forms field bound with `[formField]` to a native number-backed input gets `Infinity` or `-Infinity` as its model value, `setNativeNumberControlValue` writes it to `element.valueAsNumber`. Browsers throw a `TypeError` for infinite values, so the input keeps its old value and the rest of the view update is skipped.

I started from #72157 and checked it against the code.

Fixes #72157

## What is the new behavior?

`setNativeNumberControlValue` already writes `''` for `NaN`. It now does the same for any non-finite value (`!Number.isFinite(value)`), so `Infinity` and `-Infinity` clear the input like `NaN` does and nothing is thrown. The model value is not changed.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

### How I found it

I read `setNativeNumberControlValue` in `packages/forms/signals/src/directive/native.ts` after seeing #72157. It handles `NaN` but passes every other number straight to `valueAsNumber`.

### Where this can show up in practice

#72157 is a field report: a computed value such as `total / count` becomes `Infinity` when `count` is 0. The same helper is used for `type="range"` and the date/time inputs that take a number model.

### Verification (macOS)

`bazelisk test //packages/forms/signals/test/web:test` (Chromium and Firefox).

- New test in `number_input.spec.ts`: sets the model to `Infinity`, then `7`, then `-Infinity`, and checks the input value and the model value each time.
  - Without the fix: Chromium 407 passed, 1 failed (`Failed to set the 'valueAsNumber' property on 'HTMLInputElement': The value provided is infinite.`); Firefox 403 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped (`HTMLInputElement.valueAsNumber setter: Value being assigned is infinite.`).
  - With the fix: Chromium 408 passed, 0 failed; Firefox 404 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped.
- The existing `NaN` tests pass before and after.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(forms): clear native number inputs for infinite signal form values" (#72158)

Issues.Title: forms (signals): number, range and datetime-local bindings throw a TypeError when the model value is Infinity, and the input is left stale
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

When the model value of a Signal Forms field that is bound with `[formField]` to `<input type="number">` (also `type="range"` and `type="datetime-local"`) becomes `Infinity` or `-Infinity`, the binding throws a `TypeError` from `HTMLInputElement.valueAsNumber`.

Expected: `Infinity` is handled like `NaN`. The input is cleared and no error is thrown.

Actual: the error is thrown inside the binding. The input keeps its old value while the model holds `Infinity`, and the update of the rest of the component's view is skipped: an interpolation such as `{{ model().average }}` still shows the old value until the next change detection.

Steps:
1. A model `{ total: 10, count: 4, average: 0 }`, `form(model)`, and three `<input type="number" [formField]="...">`.
2. A button that sets `average = total / count`.
3. Click it with count 4: average becomes 2.5 in the model and in the input.
4. Set count to 0 and click again: 10 / 0 is `Infinity`.
5. Result: the error below in the console, the input still shows 2.5, and the text that prints the model still shows 2.5. A second click makes the text show `Infinity` while the input stays at 2.5.

`NaN` (0 / 0) works: the input is cleared with no error. Only `Infinity` and `-Infinity` are missing.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/Dev199092/signal-forms-infinity-repro

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
ERROR TypeError: Failed to set the 'valueAsNumber' property on 'HTMLInputElement': The value provided is infinite.
    at setNativeNumberControlValue
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular CLI       : 22.3.0
Angular           : 22.3.0
Node.js           : 24.20.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64

Browser: Chrome (also reproduced in a production build)

Package                   Installed Version
@angular/common           22.3.0
@angular/compiler         22.3.0
@angular/core             22.3.0
@angular/forms            22.3.0
@angular/platform-browser 22.3.0
```

### Anything else?

Cause: `setNativeNumberControlValue` in `packages/forms/signals/src/directive/native.ts` only guards `isNaN(value)` and otherwise does `element.valueAsNumber = value`. Browsers throw for non-finite values. The same code is on `main`.

Suggested fix: treat non-finite numbers like `NaN`:
if (!Number.isFinite(value)) { element.value = ''; } else { element.valueAsNumber = value; }

Workaround: write `Number.isFinite(x) ? x : NaN` into the model.

A realistic trigger is `total / count` with `count = 0`. Not tested: apps that use zone.js, other browsers.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "forms (signals): number, range and datetime-local bindings throw a TypeError when the model value is Infinity, and the input is left stale" (#72157)

Issues.Title: feat(devtools): improve hydration mismatch debugging experience
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## Summary

Improves the hydration mismatch debugging workflow in Angular DevTools without modifying existing console error message strings:

### 1. Core hydration debug metadata (`fix(core)`)
- Stores an optional, dev-mode-only `WeakRef<Node>` to the live mismatched DOM node (or the expected parent element with `isParentFallback: true` when the node is missing) and runtime `errorCode` (`NG0500` / `NG0501` / `NG0502`) on `__ngDebugHydrationInfo__`.
- Fixes embedded-view mismatch attribution (`@if`, `@for`, `@defer`) by using `lView[DECLARATION_COMPONENT_VIEW][HOST]` in `validateMatchingNode` and `validateNodeExists` instead of `lView[HOST]!` (which is `null` in embedded views).
- Passes the raw `describeDomFromNode(node)` snippet in `validateSiblingNodeExists` (`NG0501`) instead of duplicating the `Actual DOM is:` header.
- Zero production bundle impact (verified against `//packages/core/test/bundling/hydration:symbol_test`).

### 2. DevTools backend & extension overlays (`fix(devtools)`)
- Prevents `hydration-overlays.ts` from throwing `Unsupported hydration status highlighting: dehydrated` when dehydrated components (`ngh`) are present (e.g. `@defer` incremental hydration or siblings left unhydrated after an earlier mismatch).
- Includes root components (`<app-root>`) when collecting mismatch overlays.
- Highlights the exact mismatched child DOM element via `actualNode?.deref()` (falling back to `parentElement` for `Text`/`Comment` nodes, and to the component host element on older Angular versions).
- Adds optional serializable `errorCode`, `hasActualNode`, and `isParentFallback` fields to `HydrationStatus` in the protocol (never passes DOM `Node` instances over `postMessage`).
- Adds backend/extension actions to inspect the exact mismatched node in the **Elements** panel (`inspect(inspectedApplication.findHydrationMismatchNodeByPosition(...))`), highlight it on hover, or log the live DOM node to the **Console**.

### 3. DevTools UI (`feat(devtools)`)
- Moves hydration mismatch details out of the fixed-height (`[itemSize]="18"`) virtual-scroll `ng-tree-node` row (where leaf components had no expand chevron and `<pre>` blocks broke row heights) into a dedicated `<ng-hydration-error-view>` inside the property pane.
  - Highlights the `<-- AT THIS LOCATION` line inside `Expected DOM` / `Actual DOM` snippets.
  - Shows an error code pill with a direct link to the error reference doc (`angular.dev/errors/NG05xx`).
  - Exposes **Inspect DOM node** (or **Inspect parent** / **Inspect host** fallback for older Angular versions) and **Log node** action buttons, highlighting the live node on hover.
- Adds a compact mismatch banner at the top of the **Components** tree to auto-expand ancestors and jump straight to the failing component(s) (with prev/next controls when multiple mismatches exist).
- Adds a toolbar toggle icon for **Show hydration overlays** when hydration is detected.
- Clarifies copy on `dehydrated` components when a mismatch exists elsewhere in the tree.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

All new fields on `__ngDebugHydrationInfo__` and `HydrationStatus` are optional, so Angular DevTools remains backward-compatible with older Angular versions.

Refs #56392
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "feat(devtools): improve hydration mismatch debugging experience" (#72156)

Issues.Title: refactor(core): disambiguate repeated node paths in hydration errors
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements: - [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md - [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) - [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) ## PR Type - [ ] Bugfix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables) - [x] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes) - [ ] Build related changes - [ ] CI related changes - [ ] Documentation content changes - [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes - [ ] Other... Please describe: ## What is the current behavior? When hydration encounters a mismatch in a template with repeated nodes, `@for` iterations, or identical branches, the error message only displays the immediate parent element and the mismatched node: - Identical sibling branches (both labelled with attributes further up the tree and unlabelled branches) are indistinguishable. - Repeated direct children (`
  • ...
    • ...
` or `@for`) show no sibling index (`child element 3 of 4`) and hide `nextSibling` behind `…`. - `class` and `style` attributes are omitted from expected `TNode` snippets (`stringifyTNodeAttrs` stops at the first `AttributeMarker`), and `stripNewlines` strips *all* spaces (`card primary` -> `cardprimary`). - `validateNodeExists` (`NG0502`), `validateSiblingNodeExists` (`NG0501`), `nodeNotFoundError`, and `nodeNotFoundAtPathError` omit the declaring component name, `Actual DOM` (on missing nodes), and `ClassDebugInfo` (`filePath:lineNumber`). - `markRNodeAsHavingHydrationMismatch` used `lView[HOST]`, which is `null` inside embedded views (`@if`/`@for`/`@defer`), dropping DevTools mismatch metadata. Related to #56392 (alternative to PR 70249; does **not** add DOM validation or empirical HTML-nesting checks). ## What is the new behavior? Improves dev-mode hydration error messages (`NG0500`, `NG0501`, `NG0502`) to pinpoint **exact** mismatch locations across repeated elements and branches without repeating large vertical ancestry trees inside both `Expected` and `Actual` snippets: - **Single compact CSS-style `DOM path:` line** (omitted for trivial single-child root mismatches; shows `Expected`/`Actual DOM path:` only when the parent diverges): - Walks across component boundaries so enclosing ancestors remain visible (e.g. `app > section.panel > user-row:nth-of-type(2) > div.name`). - Uses `#id` (safely quoting non-identifier IDs such as `[id="1"]` / `[id="-1"]`), identifying attributes (`data-testid`, `aria-label`, `name`, `role`, `type`), and up to 2 valid CSS class tokens. - Disambiguates duplicate sibling elements sharing the same base selector with `:nth-of-type(N)` (e.g. `li.row:nth-of-type(3)` inside `@for`, or `section:nth-of-type(2)` for unlabelled branches). - Appends a 1-based sibling position (`(child element 3 of 4)` / `(child node 2 of 3)`) when the mismatched node sits inside a parent with multiple siblings. - Compacts deeply nested paths (`> 8` segments) by preserving notable landmarks (`#id`, identifying attributes, component hosts, and `:nth-of-type(N)` branches) instead of blindly slicing the tail. - Keeps DevTools `expectedNodeDetails` / `actualNodeDetails` compact (`

- **Symmetric surrounding sibling snippets**: `describeDomFromNode` shows both `previousSibling` and `nextSibling`, and both expected/actual snippets omit spurious leading/trailing `…` when no extra siblings exist.
- **Missing-node `Actual DOM is:`**: Shows the actual parent element contents when `node === null` (`NG0500` and `NG0502`).
- **Template `class`/`style` and preserved whitespace**: Includes static `classesWithoutHost`/`stylesWithoutHost` in expected DOM snippets and collapses whitespace runs to single spaces in `shorten()`.

Issues.Title: feat(forms): add `derive()` schema rule for signal forms
Issues.Body:
## Description

Draft prototype proposing a declarative `derive()` schema rule in `@angular/forms/signals` to address #65467 (updating a form field's value from other fields or external signals without user-written `effect()` blocks).

### Proposed API

Two progressive overloads matching existing rules (`validate`, `min`, `disabled`, `validateAsync`) and Angular's `linkedSignal` mental model:

```ts
form(model, (p) => {
  // 1. Shorthand (reactive computation; `linkedSignal(fn)` semantics)
  derive(p.total, ({valueOf}) => valueOf(p.quantity) * valueOf(p.unitPrice));

  // 2. Shorthand + config
  derive(p.slug, ({valueOf}) => slugify(valueOf(p.title)), {
    when: ({state}) => !state.dirty(),
  });

  // 3. Source-driven options (`source` tracked, `compute` runs untracked)
  derive(p.state, {
    source: p.country, // accepts SchemaPath, LogicFn, or Signal
    on: 'change', // preserves initial/hydrated value; narrows `ctx.previous` as defined
    fieldState: 'reset', // clears dirty/touched/parseErrors when updated
    compute: (country, {previous}) =>
      statesByCountry[country]?.includes(previous.value) ? previous.value : '',
  });
});
```

#### Config options
- **`when`**: Reactive guard (`LogicFn<TValue, boolean, TPathKind>`). Inactive rules do not evaluate `source`/`compute`.
- **`on`**: `'always'` (default, runs eagerly on setup and on changes / re-activation) or `'change'` (captures first active snapshot as baseline, only writes on subsequent changes; TypeScript narrows `ctx.previous` to non-nullable `{source, value}`).
- **`equal`**: Custom `ValueEqualityFn<TValue>` for comparing target values (defaults to `Object.is`).
- **`sourceEqual`**: Custom `ValueEqualityFn<TSource>` for comparing successive `source` values (defaults to `Object.is`).
- **`fieldState`**: Interaction state behavior on write — `'preserve'` (default), `'reset'` (clears `dirty`, `touched`, parse errors and cascades to descendants), or `'dirty'`.

### Key Behavioral Details
- **Schema composability**: Stored in `LogicContainer.derivations` so `schema()`, `apply()`, `applyEach()`, `applyWhen()`, `applyWhenValue()`, and recursive schemas compose and gate automatically. Subtrees with no `derive()` rules stay lazily unmaterialized.
- **Multiple rules per field**: Coexist in declaration order (`trim` → `toLowerCase` → `slice` pipeline, or multiple triggers driving the same field).
- **Availability states**: Unlike validators, `derive()` continues to run when a field is `readonly`, `disabled`, or `hidden` (enabling `readonly(p.total)` + `derive(p.total, ...)` and clearing hidden fields).
- **Execution timing (hybrid)**:
  - Runs eagerly on `form()` construction (so SSR and initial reads are settled immediately).
  - Flushes synchronously on `FieldTree` value writes (`.value.set` / `.update` / `controlValue.set`) and inside `submit()` (before validity checks and `action`).
  - Installs a single managed `effect()` on `FormFieldManager` (only when the schema has `derive()` rules) to catch direct `model.set()` calls, external signal changes, and legacy `FormControl` updates under `compatForm()`.
- **`reset(value)`**: Re-baselines `on: 'change'` rules inside the reset subtree so loading a new snapshot (e.g. `form().reset({country: 'CA', state: 'ON'})`) does not wipe `'ON'`, while `on: 'always'` rules still settle.
- **Array element identity**: Copies the parent's tracking `identitySymbol` when replacing an array item object so `FieldNode` identity (`dirty`, `touched`, bindings) is preserved.
- **Mutual pairs & cycles**: Suppresses bounce-backs into wave origin fields (preventing rounding drift in bidirectional pairs such as `celsius ↔ fahrenheit`) and throws `NG01922` (`RuntimeErrorCode.DERIVATION_CYCLE`) on non-converging cycles.

### Open Discussion Points
1. Naming: `derive` vs `derived` vs `compute` / `link`, and `compute` vs `computation` (mirroring `linkedSignal`).
2. Whether `compute` in the `{source, compute}` form should run **untracked** (implemented here to prevent accidental self-triggers) or **tracked** (matching `linkedSignal`).
3. Whether `source` should accept bare `SchemaPath` shorthand (`source: p.country`) vs strictly `LogicFn` (`({valueOf}) => valueOf(p.country)`).
4. `fieldState: 'reset'` when the newly derived value happens to equal the existing value (`equal(current, next) === true`).
5. Hybrid synchronous flush vs effect-only flush.

### Verification
- `//packages/forms/signals/test/node:test` (51 new specs in `derive.spec.ts` + `logic_node.spec.ts` + compile-time assertions in `types.spec.ts`)
- `//packages/forms:forms_api` & `//packages/forms:forms_errors` (updated `goldens/public-api/forms/signals/index.api.md`)
- `//packages/forms/signals/test/web:test_lib` build verified
- `//packages/core/test/bundling/forms_signals:symbol_test` (0 new symbols — derivation runtime is tree-shaken via `DerivationDriver` when `derive()` is unused)

Refs #65467

Issues.Title: fix(forms): throw on unimplemented methods in InteropNgControl
Issues.Body:
## Description

Addresses the first step of #69678.

When components or `ControlValueAccessor` implementations inject `NgControl` under Signal Forms (`[formField]`), an instance of `InteropNgControl` is provided via DI.
Previously, only a subset of properties/methods were implemented on `InteropNgControl`. When consumer components attempted to access common APIs (such as `statusChanges`, `valueChanges`, or `reset`), they encountered silent `undefined` or generic JavaScript runtime errors (such as `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'subscribe')`), creating a sharp developer edge without clear guidance.

### Changes in this PR:
1. Updated `CombinedControl` to declare all public properties and methods of `NgControl` (and its base `AbstractControlDirective`), with compile-time static type assertion (`Exclude<keyof NgControl, keyof CombinedControl> extends never`) to guarantee complete coverage.
2. Implemented all previously missing `NgControl` / `AbstractControlDirective` members on `InteropNgControl` to throw a descriptive `RuntimeError` (`RuntimeErrorCode.UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE`) in development mode when accessed or called, explaining that the feature is not supported by the fake `NgControl` provided by Signal Forms.
3. Added tests in `interop.spec.ts` verifying that accessing unimplemented properties/methods on `ngControl` and `ngControl.control` throws the expected `RuntimeError`.

Part of #69678

Issues.Title: fix(core): report nullish item when @for track expression throws
Issues.Body: **This is a follow-up to NG0957** (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/fee6dbf5264a30a80dfbe6b1babb7dc53215512d), which came out of a real production crash in our app, not from scanning Angular's issue tracker for something to fix. After that fix I read through the rest of the `@for` runtime looking for other places that throw without a code, and this is what turned up. Same code path, same failure mode, and the same unreadable report in a production build. It reproduces on demand; the tests in this PR fail without the change. Consider the following template: ```html @for (row of rows(); track row.Id) { {{ row.Id }} } ``` If `rows()` holds a null or an undefined at some index, the track function reads `Id` off it and throws. That function is generated by the compiler, and in a production build nothing survives that identifies it. `_forTrack0` is a module local arrow, so the build mangles it to two letters, and the frames under it mangle too. This is the whole report: ``` TypeError Cannot read properties of null (reading 'Id') at Qe(https://some-site.com/chunk-BTt5Der3.js:4:9467) at Ha(https://some-site.com/chunk-B9SSlBOH.js:4:8763) at _T(https://some-site.com/chunk-B9SSlBOH.js:4:8920) at kT(https://some-site.com/chunk-B9SSlBOH.js:4:13077) at template(https://some-site.com/chunk-BTt5Der3.js:2:28442) ``` There is no error code to search for, no mention of `@for`, and no component name. `Qe` is the track function and `template` is the component, both in a feature chunk; the three frames between them are `valuesMatching`, `reconcile` and `ɵɵrepeater`. Nothing in the report says so. The only usable signal is the property name in the message, and a chunk often holds several `@for` blocks tracking by the same property. With this fix `ɵɵrepeater` catches the error and looks at the collection for a nullish item. If it finds one, it throws NG0958 and keeps the original error in `cause`. Everything else is rethrown unchanged. The success path is untouched: the only addition is a `catch` on a block that already needed a `finally`. The track function is only compared here, never called again. Calling user code from inside an error handler can throw a second time, and nothing says that a track expression is free of side effects. Even `track counter++` compiles. So the check reads the data instead. Errors that already carry a code pass through untouched, the same way `encapsulateBoundaryError` leaves them alone. A nullish item also cannot be the cause when the track expression is `$index` or the item itself, so those pass through too. The check is a heuristic and it states only what it saw, that the item is nullish. A track expression that fails on a real object, say a throwing getter, still reports the plain TypeError. It can also point at the wrong thing: if the loop body throws from a component constructor and the collection happens to hold a nullish item elsewhere, the nullish item is what gets named. `cause` carries the original error in that case. This is also the first track diagnostic that throws. The other two, NG0955 and NG0956, warn in dev only. There is no open issue for this. We found it while auditing the rest of the `@for` runtime after NG0957.

Issues.Title: URL serializer drops query and matrix parameters named `__proto__`
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

router

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

writing{variant="document" id="63183"}
### Description

Angular Router's `DefaultUrlSerializer` silently drops URL query parameters and matrix parameters whose key is `__proto__`.

This happens because the parser uses ordinary JavaScript objects (`{}`) as parameter accumulators. When a parameter with the key `__proto__` is assigned, JavaScript invokes the inherited `Object.prototype.__proto__` setter instead of creating an own property.

As a result, the parameter is lost during URL parsing.

### Steps to reproduce

**1. Query parameter**

```typescript
import { DefaultUrlSerializer } from '@angular/router';

const serializer = new DefaultUrlSerializer();
const tree = serializer.parse('/path?__proto__=value&normal=hello');

console.log(tree.queryParamMap.has('__proto__')); // false
console.log(tree.queryParamMap.get('__proto__')); // null
console.log(tree.queryParamMap.get('normal'));    // hello
```

**2. Matrix parameter**

```typescript
const tree = serializer.parse('/path;__proto__=value;normal=hello');

const segment = tree.root.children['primary'].segments[0];

console.log(segment.parameterMap.has('__proto__')); // false
console.log(segment.parameterMap.get('__proto__')); // null
console.log(segment.parameterMap.get('normal'));    // hello
```

### Expected behavior

Angular Router should preserve `__proto__` as an ordinary URL parameter key.

- Query parameters named `__proto__` should be accessible through `queryParamMap`.
- Matrix parameters named `__proto__` should be accessible through `parameterMap`.
- Serializing and parsing the URL again should preserve these parameters.
- Duplicate query parameters with this key should retain the expected array behavior.
- Normal URL parameters should continue working as before.

### Actual behavior

Both query and matrix parameters named `__proto__` are silently discarded during parsing.

Other parameter keys, such as `normal`, are parsed correctly.

### Technical details

The issue originates in:

- `parseQueryParams()` — initializes its accumulator using `{}`.
- `parseMatrixParams()` — also initializes its accumulator using `{}`.

Both functions assign decoded parameter keys directly to these objects.

The existing `parseParens()` implementation already uses `Object.create(null)` to avoid the same special-key behavior for outlet names.

### Suggested approach

Use null-prototype objects (`Object.create(null)`) for the query and matrix parameter accumulators.

This allows `__proto__` to be stored as an ordinary own property without changing the public Router APIs.

### Additional information

I have prepared five regression tests covering:

1. Parsing a query parameter named `__proto__`.
2. Query parameter serialization and parsing round-trip.
3. Duplicate `__proto__` query parameters.
4. Parsing a matrix parameter named `__proto__`.
5. Preserving normal parameters alongside `__proto__`.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

_No response_

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true

```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular CLI: 22.3.0
Angular: 22.4.0-next.0 (framework monorepo source)
Node.js: 24.18.0
Package Manager: pnpm 12.21.0
Operating System: Windows 11 (win32 x64)
```

### Anything else?

Issues.Title: fix(router): preserve `__proto__` query and matrix parameters
Issues.Body:
## Description

This PR fixes an issue where Angular Router's `DefaultUrlSerializer` silently drops query and matrix parameters whose key is `__proto__`.

The issue occurs because `parseQueryParams()` and `parseMatrixParams()` use ordinary `{}` objects as parameter accumulators. Assigning a value to the `__proto__` key invokes the inherited setter on `Object.prototype` instead of creating an own property.

### Changes made

- Changed the query parameter accumulator in `parseQueryParams()` to use `Object.create(null)`.
- Changed the matrix parameter accumulator in `parseMatrixParams()` to use `Object.create(null)`.
- Added five regression tests covering:
  - Parsing a query parameter named `__proto__`.
  - Query parameter serialization and parsing round-trip.
  - Duplicate `__proto__` query parameters.
  - Parsing a matrix parameter named `__proto__`.
  - Preserving normal parameters alongside `__proto__`.

### Implementation details

The fix follows the existing null-prototype object pattern already used in `parseParens()` and `squashSegmentGroup()`.

No public APIs or unrelated Router behavior have been changed.

### Testing

- Added five regression tests in `packages/router/test/url_tree.spec.ts`.
- Performed local Node.js validation: 21 assertions passed.
- `git diff --check` completed without errors.

Fixes #72150

Issues.Title: animate.enter and (animate.enter) replay enter animations on already-rendered DOM during SSR client hydration
Issues.Body:
When an SSR application uses `provideClientHydration()`, elements and component hosts (including bootstrapped roots and hydrated `<router-outlet>` components) that were already rendered in the server HTML and reused in place during client hydration still trigger `animate.enter` (and `(animate.enter)` callbacks) on bootstrap, causing visible flash/re-entry animations on static SSR content (and similarly when `@defer (hydrate on ...)` blocks incrementally hydrate).

Before submitting a fix (cc @jessicajaniuk @alxhub), could we confirm the intended semantics on two edge cases:
1. Should `(animate.enter)` JS callbacks be suppressed alongside `animate.enter` class bindings on hydrated nodes (since `(animate.enter)`'s `animationComplete()` is a no-op and third-party WAAPI/GSAP callbacks otherwise replay the same flash on hydrated DOM, while subsequent client-side insertions like `@if`/`@for`/router navigations still fire both)?
2. For `ngSkipHydration` components, where Angular reuses the host element itself but clears and re-creates its subtree from scratch on the client, should `animate.enter` be skipped on the reused host element while still running on the newly client-rendered children inside the skipped subtree?

Issues.Title: fix(core): release leavingNodes when animate.leave resolves to no classes
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

When an element with an `[animate.leave]` binding is detached, `node_manipulation` eagerly calls `trackLeavingNodes(tNode, rNode, parentLView)`. If `runLeaveAnimations` subsequently resolves an empty class list (`''`, `'   '`, `[]`, `null`, `undefined`), it pushes a resolver onto `LView`'s leave animation entry, adds `lView[ID]` to `allLeavingAnimations`, and immediately calls `resolve()` without running `animateLeaveClassRunner`.

Because `clearLeavingNodes` is only called by `animateLeaveClassRunner` and `leaveAnimationFunctionCleanup`, the `{el, declarationView}` entry remains retained in the module-level `leavingNodes` `WeakMap` for the lifetime of the `TNode`, leaking every detached element and its declaration view. A similar leak also occurred if `injector.get(ANIMATION_QUEUE)` threw (e.g. during `ApplicationRef` teardown) after `trackLeavingNodes` had already been called.

Issue Number: #72141

## What is the new behavior?

- In `runLeaveAnimations`, only push to `resolvers` and add `lView[ID]` to `allLeavingAnimations` when `activeClasses` is non-empty.
- In `node_animations` (inside the tree-shaken animation runtime), clear the tracked `leavingNodes` entry for `(tNode, rNode)` once leave animations settle or when the animation queue cannot be resolved / no animations run. Clearing at settlement rather than inside `runLeaveAnimations`'s empty-class branch preserves `leavingNodes` tracking and `declarationView` when an empty `[animate.leave]` is composed with an active `animate.leave` on the same element or when a descendant has an active leave animation.
- In `cancelLeavingNodes`, delete the `tNode` entry from `leavingNodes` once its array becomes empty.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Fixes #72141

Issues.Title: docs(core): correct forwardRef usage in standalone example
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines.
- [ ] Tests for the changes have been added (documentation-only change; no tests required).
- [x] Docs have been added / updated.

## PR Type

- [x] Documentation content changes

## What is the current behavior?

The `Circle standalone reference import example` uses `forwardRef` on `ChildComponent` to reference `ParentComponent`.

However, `ParentComponent` is declared before `ChildComponent`, so the reference to `ParentComponent` is already available when the `ChildComponent` decorator is evaluated.

At the same time, `ChildComponent` is referenced in the `ParentComponent` decorator before its declaration, which requires `forwardRef`.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

Move `forwardRef` to the `ParentComponent` imports to defer the reference to `ChildComponent`, which has not yet been declared.

Use a direct reference to `ParentComponent` in the `ChildComponent` imports, since it has already been declared.

This makes the example consistent with the declaration order of the components and correctly demonstrates the use of `forwardRef` in circular standalone component imports.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Same aplies to https://angular.dev/api/core/forwardRef

Issues.Title: feat(forms): support binding numeric values to `<select>` in signal forms
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Bugfix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Native `<select [formField]="...">` elements in Signal Forms only accept `string` models. Attempting to bind a `number` or `number | null` model fails template type-checking, and the runtime reads/writes `<select>` values strictly as strings (including inside the `MutationObserver` re-sync callback).

Issue Number: Refs #68217

## What is the new behavior?

Native single-select `<select [formField]="...">` elements now support binding either `string` subtypes (string, string literal unions, string enums, `T extends string`) **or** `number | null` subtypes (`number`, `number | null`, numeric literal unions, numeric enums, `T extends number | null`):

- **Template type-checking (`TcbNativeFieldOp`)**: checks the field's value signal against `(() => string) | (() => number | null)`.
  - Covariant `(() => string)` preserves full backwards compatibility with existing string literal unions, string enums, and generic string-constrained fields.
  - Covariant `(() => number | null)` supports non-nullable `number`, `number | null`, numeric literal unions, and numeric enums.
  - Because function return types do not distribute across the union, mixed models (`string | null`, `string | number`, `string | number | null`) are strictly rejected at compile time, keeping `null` unambiguous at runtime.
- **Runtime (`native.ts` & `control_native.ts`)**:
  - Uses `isSelect(element) && !element.multiple` (works in both browsers and Domino/SSR, where `HTMLSelectElement.type` is `undefined`).
  - `getNativeControlValue`: if the current model value is `number` or `null`, parses `''` as `null`, valid numeric strings via `Number(...)`, and non-numeric or whitespace-only values as `NativeInputParseError`. `string` models continue to return `element.value` unchanged.
  - `setNativeControlValue`: writes numeric values via `String(value)` and converts `NaN` and `null` to `''`.
  - `observeSelectMutations`: re-syncs via `setNativeControlValue(...)` so dynamically added `<option>` elements properly select numeric, `null`, and `NaN` values.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

All existing type-checked `<select [formField]>` usages (including string literal unions, string enums, and generic string-constrained fields) continue to compile and behave identically at runtime.

## Other information

- Related to #68217.
- Also related to existing draft PR #68442 (which allowed `string | number | null` covariantly, creating ambiguity for `string | null` models).

Issues.Title: [Feature request]: Resource based suspense with @await blocks in @boundary
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request? core, compiler, compiler-cli, router, common, platform-server ### Description **Builds on:** - `@boundary` / `@error` (developer preview, 22.2) - `resource()` - Router resources (developer preview, 22.2) - Router error boundaries (developer preview, 22.3) **Scope:** compiler, template syntax, runtime (render3), resource and input types, router integration, DevTools > Implementation notes and prior art (React Suspense, Solid 2.0, the router precedents) are in the first comment, to keep this body within GitHub's size limit. #### 1. Summary This proposal adds **coordinated loading states** to Angular templates. It extends the existing `@boundary` error boundary, so the same block that catches errors also manages pending data. It has three parts: 1. **The `@await` block.** A template block that unwraps one or more resources into plain values. Inside the block, the values have their loaded type, not `T | undefined`. The block registers its resources with the nearest boundary. Its content renders, and later updates, only when the resources are ready. 2. **A `@pending` block on `@boundary`.** The `@pending` block is the fallback. A boundary that has a `@pending` block coordinates every `@await` registered below it. It reveals them together, keeps stale content on screen while they refresh, and resets when the content's identity changes (`track`). It also exposes a `$pending` context variable. 3. **Configuration.** `provideBoundaries()` sets app-wide defaults for timing in core. In the router, `withBoundaries()` combines today's error options with pending coordination at each ``. ```html @boundary (track userId(); let refreshing = $pending) { @if (refreshing) { } @await (user = userResource; posts = feedResource) {

{{ user.name }}

} } @pending (after 150ms; minimum 400ms) { } @error (let e; reset = $reset) { } ``` Suspension is **explicit**. A resource only takes part when it is read through `@await`. Reading `resource.value()` directly behaves as it does today. Angular's signal graph does not change: pending and error stay properties of the resource object, not hidden state in the graph. #### 2. Motivation ##### 2.1 The problem today Resources made async data first-class in Angular. Each resource exposes `value()`, `status()`, `error()`, `isLoading()`, `hasValue()` and `snapshot()`. Every template that reads a resource handles those states itself, which leads to the following problems. - **Loading-state sprawl.** Each component writes its own `@if (res.isLoading())` and `@if (res.error())` branches. A page with five resources shows five spinners that appear and disappear independently. - **Inconsistent states on screen (tearing).** When a resource reloads, parts of the UI that depend on it update at different times. A header can show the new user while a sibling list still shows the previous user's data. - **Flashing.** Reloads that resolve quickly make spinners flash. A new request clears a resource's value, so content that depends on it disappears and the layout jumps. - **No coordination across components.** Resources are often created or injected several components deep. Showing one fallback for a section means passing loading signals up through inputs and outputs. For resources injected through DI, that wiring doesn't exist at all. - **`T | undefined` everywhere.** Without a `defaultValue`, `value()` is `T | undefined`. Templates fill up with `?.` and `@if (res.hasValue())` guards, even in areas that only make sense once the data is ready. A `defaultValue` removes `undefined` from the type, but templates then show the default (for example an empty list) as if it were data while loading. - **Errors are handled separately from loading.** `@boundary` already catches resource errors, because `value()` throws in the error state. It knows nothing about pending state, so loading and error handling are written in two different ways. - **Non-blocking route data flashes.** When a `nonBlocking()` route resource's params change on navigation, the new request clears its value, and the page flashes ([#70809](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/70809)). - The maintainers' answers were to use a blocking resource, or to keep the previous value with a snapshot in userland. They noted that the router has no opinion on how the transition should look, and that keeping old values would be "very incorrect for many situations", for example "showing data for /user/1 after navigation to /user/2 is complete". Suspense and transitions were mentioned in passing; the suggested mitigation was a `waitFor` option ([PR #70539](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/70539)). - The choice between keeping old content and showing a placeholder belongs to a specific area of UI, which neither the router nor the resource knows about. Whatever that area chooses, it must never show data for a different route (§5.6). ##### 2.2 What Angular already coordinates, and where it stops Angular already provides coordination, freezing and fallback UI, but only at the router level: - **Route-level coordination.** Router resources (`withRouterResources()`, `Route.resources`) load in parallel across the matched route hierarchy. By default they are *blocking*: the router waits for them before activating the route, and the component receives a plain `T`. - **Freezing during navigation.** While a navigation is pending, resources on `ActivatedRoute` show the state they had when the navigation started. The previous screen stays stable until the navigation commits or is rolled back. - **Error fallbacks at the outlet.** Router error boundaries (`withErrorBoundaries()`, `Route.errorComponent`) replace a failed routed component with a fallback component. None of these reach below the outlet. Once a route is active, component-owned resources, non-blocking route resources and refreshes that happen without a navigation have no coordination, no freezing and no shared fallback. This proposal brings the same guarantees to any part of a template: | Router level (exists) | Template level (proposed) | |---|---| | Router coordinates route data across the route hierarchy | `@boundary` coordinates resources across nested components | | Blocking resources delay route activation | `@await` delays rendering of data-dependent content | | `nonBlocking()` hands loading state to the component | `@pending` gives a coordinated fallback for that state | | Route resources frozen during navigation | Revealed content kept on screen during any refresh | | `errorComponent` handles failures of the routed component | `@error` handles failures local to a boundary | The two levels complement each other. The router stays responsible for navigation-time data, and boundaries take over once the route is active (§5.6). ##### 2.3 Why this needs the framework Userland can't build this correctly, for these reasons. - **Block syntax can't be extended.** `@boundary` is compiler syntax and accepts no parameters today. Userland can't add `@pending` or new parameters to it. - **Freezing needs view ownership.** Freezing content means skipping the update pass of views you don't own. With ``, the content's views belong to the parent, so a wrapper component can't freeze them. - **No commit phase.** Angular's template instructions write to the DOM as they run. Avoiding half-updated views needs a compiler guarantee that every operand of a block is evaluated before any binding in that block. - **Correct types need the compiler.** The type checker has to know that the block's content only runs when the value has loaded. - **Parallel loading needs runtime control.** A component's `resource()` starts its request from an effect tied to the view that declares the component. Starting nested components' requests before the parent's data has resolved ("create early, bind late", §5.5) means running those effects while skipping the view's bindings. Only change detection can do that. #### 3. Goals and non-goals ##### Goals - **Explicit opt-in.** Suspension happens only where `@await` is written. - **Coordination across components.** Resources read anywhere below a boundary, at any depth and however they were obtained (input, DI, local field), take part in the same pending state. - **One place for policy.** Fallback, timing, stale-content limits and identity resets live on `@boundary` and `@pending`. - **All-or-nothing updates.** No `@await` block is ever half-updated, and blocks under the same boundary are revealed and released together. - **Parallel data loading.** Nesting components inside `@await` must not turn independent requests into a waterfall. - **Typed values.** Values unwrapped by `@await` have the resource's loaded type. - **Easy to inspect.** DevTools and diagnostics show which resources hold which boundary, and why. ##### Non-goals - Implicit pending propagation through the signal graph (§10.1). - Changing how the router handles navigation-time data. Blocking route resources, navigation freezing and `NavigationError` keep their current behaviour. - Suspending on raw Promises or Observables. Resources are the supported protocol, and `rxResource`, `httpResource` and similar adapters cover other sources. - Suspending code in the component class (computeds, effects, methods). Class code keeps reading resources as it does today. - A programmatic API for boundaries (§11). - Replacing `@defer`. `@defer` controls *when code loads and when views are created*. Suspense controls *when data-dependent content is revealed or updated*. ### Proposed solution #### 4. Design overview | Concern | Construct | Placed | |---|---|---| | Unwrapping data, all-or-nothing updates | `@await (x = res; …) { }` | Deep, where data is read | | Fallback, timing, stale-content limit, identity, grouping | `@boundary (…) { } @pending (…) { } @error { }` | High, at layout or section level | | App-wide defaults | `provideBoundaries()`, router `withBoundaries()` | Application config | The split is deliberate. `@await` blocks are **local**: each one unwraps values and freezes its own small area. A `@boundary` with `@pending` **coordinates**: it groups every `@await` registered beneath it, decides what users see while they are pending, and releases them together. Two pieces of data are "part of the same suspense" when they are registered with the same boundary, not when they appear in the same block. Component authors and library authors follow one rule: **put `@await` where you read the data.** The block joins whatever boundary the consumer placed around the component. Nothing else is needed. #### 5. Detailed design ##### 5.1 The `@await` block ###### Syntax ```html @await (alias = expression; alias2 = expression2) { …content using alias and alias2… } ``` - One or more `alias = expression` pairs, separated by semicolons. - Aliases are scoped to the block's content, like `@if (…; as x)`. - **Operands are independent.** An operand can't refer to another alias in the same header, and the compiler reports an error if it does, so no operand waits on another alias. Data that depends on another alias goes in a nested block, which makes the dependency visible in the template: ```html @await (user = userResource) { @await (posts = user.feedResource) { … } } ``` - `@await` has no `@pending` or `@error` blocks of its own. Fallbacks and errors belong to the boundary. ###### Accepted operands An operand must be **resource-shaped**, which is checked structurally: ```ts interface ResourceLike { readonly snapshot: Signal>; readonly [ɵRESOURCE_LOADED]?: readonly [L]; // type-only marker, see "Typing" reload?(): boolean; } ``` - **`snapshot`** reads the status and the value together and never throws. `Resource` already exposes it, so `resource`, `rxResource`, `httpResource`, `resourceFromSnapshots`, router resources and userland wrappers all qualify without a framework brand. - **`reload()` is optional**, because the read-only types (`Resource`, and the type `asReadonly()` returns) don't declare it, and userland wrappers may not have one. It is only used by `$reset` (§5.2.7). - **Compile time.** The generated type-check code passes each operand through an intrinsic, `ɵawait()`. Anything that isn't resource-shaped is a template type error. - **Runtime (dev mode).** A shape check produces a clear error for operands that get past type checking, for example through `any`. - **Plain signals, Promises and Observables are rejected.** None of them has a `snapshot`. - A `Signal` is never pending, so awaiting one would quietly do nothing. - A Promise has no synchronous status, and its identity is not stable across checks. ###### Typing Inside the content, each alias has the resource's **loaded type**: the type its loader produces, without the `undefined` that the resource adds while nothing has loaded. Today that distinction is lost. A resource without `defaultValue` is typed `ResourceRef`, which is the same for a loader returning `Promise` and one returning `Promise`. This proposal keeps it with a second, defaulted type parameter on the resource types: ```ts interface Resource { readonly [ɵRESOURCE_LOADED]?: readonly [L]; // value, status, error, isLoading, snapshot and hasValue are unchanged } // overload without defaultValue function resource(options: ResourceOptions): ResourceRef; ``` ```ts userResource = resource({loader: () => fetchUser()}); // ResourceRef maybeUser = resource({loader: () => findUser()}); // ResourceRef hits = resource({loader: () => search(), defaultValue: []}); // ResourceRef ``` ```html @await (u = userResource) { … } @await (m = maybeUser) { … } @await (h = hits) { … } ``` - **When the marker is missing**, the alias has the resource's `T`, which is always sound. This covers userland wrappers without the marker, and user annotations such as `input>()`. A child component's input keeps the loaded type when it is declared as `Resource`. - **Known gap:** calling `set(undefined)` on a writable resource whose loaded type excludes `undefined` produces a `local` resource holding `undefined`. The block still renders it, and dev mode warns (§5.8). ###### When a block is ready Readiness depends only on the resource's **status**, never on `hasValue()`. A `defaultValue` makes `hasValue()` true while loading, but it is not loaded data. | Status | Before the block's first reveal | After the block has been revealed | |---|---|---| | `resolved`, `local` | **Ready** | **Ready**: the content updates | | `loading`, `reloading` | **Waiting** | **Refreshing**: the boundary's stale policy applies (§5.2.4) | | `idle` | **Hidden**: doesn't hold the boundary | **Hidden**: content kept alive off-screen; doesn't hold the boundary | | `error` | **Error** (§5.2.7) | **Error** (§5.2.7) | - **`reloading` waits before the first reveal.** A resource can be `reloading` after an error, when it has no value. A block created while a shared resource reloads waits for the fresh value instead of showing an old one. - **`idle` means "no data requested",** for example a search with an empty query, so the block shows nothing and doesn't hold its boundary. "Not available yet" is expressed by `params` throwing `ResourceParamsStatus.LOADING` (§5.5), which makes the resource `loading`. Authors who want an empty state write it outside the block: ```html @if (results.status() === 'idle') {

Type to search

} @await (r = results) { } ``` - **A hidden block that starts loading** follows its boundary's phase (§5.2.2). It holds the reveal while the boundary is pending, and it is a late block, hidden until ready, while the boundary shows content. ###### Semantics 1. **Unit of freezing.** Each control-flow block has its own embedded view, and the `@await` content view is the unit that renders or freezes. While the block is waiting or refreshing, its content's bindings are not updated, apart from early inputs (§5.5). Content outside the block, including siblings in the same template, is unaffected. 2. **All-or-nothing.** All operands are read before any binding in the content, so the content is never half-updated against a mix of old and new values. 3. **Registration.** When it is created, the block registers its operands with the nearest coordinating boundary (§5.2.8). It re-registers when an operand's identity changes, and unregisters when it is destroyed. 4. **Typing guarantee.** The content's bindings only run in the *ready* state, so an alias always holds loaded data. 5. **Per-row suspension.** Inside `@for`, each row's `@await` registers separately (§5.2.2): ```html @for (item of items(); track item.id) { @await (details = item.detailsResource) { } } ``` ###### What `@await` does *not* do - It doesn't affect class code. A `computed` that reads `userResource.value()` still sees `undefined` (or the `defaultValue`) while loading, and rethrows in the error state. - It doesn't catch errors from non-resource sources. Existing `@boundary` error handling covers those. - It doesn't start or cancel requests. Resource lifecycles are unchanged. ##### 5.2 Pending states on `@boundary` ###### 5.2.1 Full syntax ```html @boundary (track ; let = $pending) { …content… } @pending (after ; minimum ; stale none | | unlimited) { …fallback… } @error (let e; reset = $reset; when ) { … } @error { … } ``` - Every parameter is optional, and parameters can appear in any order. - **A boundary coordinates pending state only if it has a `@pending` block.** A `@boundary` without one behaves exactly as it does today, and passes `@await` registrations up to the next coordinating boundary. - **A boundary without `@error` blocks doesn't catch errors.** Errors pass through it to the next boundary out, so a pending-only section boundary never destroys its content because of an error. This changes today's behaviour (§5.9). - **To coordinate without a fallback,** use an empty `@pending { }`. Blocks are still revealed together and stale content is still kept, but nothing is shown while the boundary is pending. ###### 5.2.2 Boundary and block states Each `@await` block and each coordinating boundary has a small set of phases. | Block phase | Meaning | |---|---| | `waiting` | Not ready and never shown. Bindings aren't applied. | | `ready` | Showing current data. | | `frozen` | Showing its last data while its resources refresh. | | `hidden` | Content kept alive but not shown: the resource is `idle`, or the block is a *late block* that isn't ready yet. | | Boundary phase | Meaning | |---|---| | `pending` | No registered block is showing content, and at least one is waiting. The fallback rules of §5.2.3 apply. | | `revealed` | The content is shown, and every showing block is ready. | | `refreshing` | The content is shown, and at least one showing block is frozen. `$pending` is `true`. | | `stale-fallback` | A refresh outlasted `stale`. The content is kept alive off the DOM, and the fallback is shown. | | `error` | An `@error` block is shown. | **"First load" is the `pending` phase**: the boundary has no block showing content. A boundary whose blocks were all hidden (for example because their resources are `idle`) is pending again when one of them starts loading. Whether "first load" should instead happen once per boundary, or be tracked per block, is open question 1 (§11). | Event | When the boundary is… | Result | |---|---|---| | A block registers, or a hidden block starts loading | `pending` | It holds the reveal. | | | `revealed` or `refreshing` | It is a **late block**: hidden until ready, sets `$pending`, doesn't hold other blocks' release, doesn't start the `stale` timer. | | A showing block's resource starts loading or reloading | `revealed` | The block freezes. The boundary moves to `refreshing`, and the `stale` timer starts. | | Every frozen block is ready | `refreshing` | All frozen blocks update **in one pass**, and the boundary moves to `revealed`. Blocks discovered during that pass are late blocks. | | `stale` elapses | `refreshing` | `stale-fallback`. | | Every non-hidden block is ready | `pending` or `stale-fallback` | The content is attached (after `minimum`), and the boundary moves to `revealed`. | | A showing block's resource becomes `idle` | any shown phase | The block is hidden and stops counting. | | The `track` value changes | any | The content is recreated, and the boundary moves to `pending`. | | A resource errors | any | The error is raised from the block's view (§5.2.7). | - **`@for` rows.** Each row's block registers separately and follows the same rules. Rows are revealed together on first load, and rows added later are late blocks. - **Hidden content** is frozen (§5.5) and kept until the block is destroyed. ###### 5.2.3 First load: `after` and `minimum` While the boundary is `pending`, it shows `@pending` instead of its content. The content is still **created** in the background (§5.5), so requests start and nested blocks are discovered. It is attached to the DOM only when every block that isn't hidden is ready, so nothing half-loaded is ever visible. - **`after `:** wait this long before showing the fallback. If everything is ready sooner, the content appears directly, with no flash. - **`minimum `:** once shown, keep the fallback on screen for at least this long, to avoid a flicker. These have the same meaning as the options on `@defer`'s `@loading` block. How the timers interact: - **An error during `minimum`** waits until `minimum` ends, as in `@defer`, so the fallback never flickers straight into an error. - **A `track` change during `after`:** the old content is already destroyed, so nothing is shown until `after` elapses, then the fallback. - **Reveal batching** (§5.4) is measured from the last reveal. The first reveal is never delayed. ###### 5.2.4 Refreshes: `stale` A **refresh** happens when a block that is showing content needs new data, for example because a registered resource's params changed or `reload()` was called. By default, the boundary **keeps the content on screen**: - Refreshing `@await` blocks are frozen and keep showing their last values. - The rest of the boundary's content keeps updating, which is what makes a "refreshing" indicator possible (§5.2.5). - `$pending` is `true`. - When every frozen block is ready again, they all update **together, in one pass**. `stale` limits how long stale content may stay on screen: ```html } @pending (after 150ms; minimum 400ms) { … } } @pending (after 150ms; minimum 400ms; stale 1s) { … } } @pending (after 150ms; minimum 400ms; stale none) { … } } @pending (stale unlimited) { … } ``` - **When the fallback replaces stale content,** the content views stay alive but are detached from the DOM. **Component state survives; DOM state may not**: focus, selection, scroll positions, `
