Issues.Title: fix(core): safely handle server platform destruction on aborted SSR requests
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

When an SSR server immediately destroys `PlatformRef` on request abort (e.g. via `@angular/ssr`), several framework paths can crash the Node.js process with `uncaughtException` or `unhandledRejection`, or leave in-flight requests open:

- `bootstrap()` looks up `ENABLE_ROOT_COMPONENT_BOOTSTRAP` after `ApplicationInitStatus.donePromise` without checking `envInjector.destroyed`, throwing `NG0205`.
- `ApplicationInitStatus` does not unsubscribe observable initializers or settle `donePromise` when destroyed.
- `INTERNAL_APPLICATION_ERROR_HANDLER` throws via `setTimeout(() => { throw e; })` when `injector.destroyed` and no prior error has cached `userErrorHandler`, terminating Node.js SSR servers.
- `PendingTasks.run()` reports post-destroy promise rejections to `ErrorHandler`.
- `FetchBackend` does not abort in-flight `fetch` requests on `DestroyRef.onDestroy`, and emitting `complete()` on stream cancellation triggers `EmptyError` in `firstValueFrom`/`lastValueFrom`.
- `Router.dispose()` does not unsubscribe active `setupNavigations` transitions, leaving guards and resolvers running after platform teardown.
- `renderInternal()` reports rejections from async `BEFORE_APP_SERIALIZED` hooks and calls `renderToString()` even if the platform was destroyed mid-hook.

Related issue: angular/angular-cli#34754

## What is the new behavior?

- **`@angular/core`**:
  - `ApplicationInitStatus` unsubscribes observable initializers on `DestroyRef.onDestroy`, settles `donePromise` without setting `done = true`, stops remaining initializers if destroyed, and ignores late post-destroy rejections.
  - `bootstrap()`, `internalCreateApplication()`, and `PlatformRef.bootstrapModule()` settle cleanly with the destroyed `ApplicationRef` / `NgModuleRef` without bootstrapping root components when destroyed before or during initialization.
  - `PendingTasks.run()` checks `DestroyRef.destroyed` before reporting errors.
  - `INTERNAL_APPLICATION_ERROR_HANDLER` logs via `console.error('ERROR', e)` on the server when destroyed without a cached `ErrorHandler` instead of throwing from `setTimeout`.
- **`@angular/common/http`**:
  - `FetchBackend` unsubscribes on `DestroyRef.onDestroy` to abort in-flight `fetch` calls and clear timeouts without emitting `complete()` or `error()`, cancels body streams on destroy, and skips initiating requests when already destroyed.
- **`@angular/router`**:
  - `Router.dispose()` unsubscribes active `setupNavigations` transitions (after detaching the navigation event listener) and `withEnabledBlockingInitialNavigation()` skips starting navigation if the injector was destroyed while awaiting `LOCATION_INITIALIZED`.
- **`@angular/platform-server`**:
  - `renderInternal()`, `renderApplication()`, and `renderModule()` return `''` early when destroyed before or during async `BEFORE_APP_SERIALIZED` hooks, suppress post-destroy `ErrorHandler` reporting, and ensure `asyncDestroyPlatform()` always resolves safely.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] No

## Other information

Companion `@angular/ssr` PR: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/pull/34768
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(core): safely handle server platform destruction on aborted SSR requests" (#72139)

Issues.Title: augmentChunkHash hashes only input source maps, so an output-map change keeps a lazy chunk name while its debugId (and bytes) change
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

The same gap exists since #34583, but it shows up on a toolchain update: 22.2.6 → 22.3.0.

### Description

#34583 made the chunk optimizer's `augmentChunkHash` include the hashes of the *input* source maps of a chunk's modules, so that a change that only affects the source map renames the chunk (#34574). The `//# debugId=` comment injected after naming is derived from the *output* source map, though, and the output map can change while every input map stays the same.

Updating `@angular/build` from 22.2.6 to 22.3.0 does exactly that for vendor-only lazy chunks. In our production build, two lazy chunks that hold only third-party code (SheetJS and jsPDF, loaded with `import()`) kept their file names, and their JavaScript was byte-for-byte identical apart from the trailing comment:

```
-//# debugId=e8aee844-1ba7-543c-be31-811b9fc51bb2
+//# debugId=fb140939-ab0f-576a-a399-540d2ee6737b
```

In the chunks' `.map` files, `sources` and `sourcesContent` are identical; only `names` and `mappings` differ (the newer minifier maps the same output differently). The input maps are unchanged, so `augmentChunkHash` returns the same value, Rolldown's code hash is the same, and the file name is the same while the bytes differ.

With `subresourceIntegrity` on, a browser or CDN that holds the old copy under that name fails the integrity check against the new `index.html`, and the lazy import fails. The same applies to any update that changes only how the output is mapped (minifier, Rolldown, or the debug ID computation), so every toolchain bump can reintroduce it.

Related: #34674 reports the same symptom for `main` and `polyfills`, and proposes naming files from their final bytes after debug IDs are injected. That approach would also cover this case; hashing the output map (or the final file contents) in `augmentChunkHash` would cover it for optimized lazy chunks.

### Minimal Reproduction

1. An application with source maps on for scripts, `subresourceIntegrity: true`, and enough lazy chunks for the chunk optimizer to run (3 or more), including at least one lazy chunk that holds only a third-party library loaded with `import('<package>')`.
2. Build with `@angular/build` 22.2.6 and keep `dist/`.
3. Update `@angular/build` and `@angular/cli` to 22.3.0 without changing application code, and build again.
4. Compare the two `dist/` folders: list files that exist in both with the same name and different contents. The vendor-only lazy chunk is among them, and `diff` shows only the `//# debugId=` line changed.

### Exception or Error

```text
Failed to find a valid digest in the 'integrity' attribute for resource '<origin>/chunk-XXXXXXXX.js' with computed SHA-384 integrity '...'. The resource has been blocked.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.3.0
@angular/build    : 22.3.0 (previous build: 22.2.6)
@angular/core     : 22.3.0
TypeScript        : 6.0.3
Node.js           : 24.22.1
Package manager   : npm 11.19
OS                : macOS and Linux (CI)

Build options: `sourceMap: true`, `subresourceIntegrity: true`, `outputHashing: all`, production configuration.

Build options: sourceMap: true, subresourceIntegrity: true, outputHashing: all, production configuration.
```

### Anything else relevant?

(The error above is the shape of the browser error when a stale cached copy is served; our CI caught the name collision before deploy, so we did not ship it.)

Workaround we used: change what the app imports from each library (a local module that re-exports only the used members), which changes the rendered chunk code and so its name. `namedChunks: true` only changes the readable prefix; the `[hash]` part is computed the same way, so it does not prevent this.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "augmentChunkHash hashes only input source maps, so an output-map change keeps a lazy chunk name while its debugId (and bytes) change" (#34774)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): validate path options against MCP roots in host execution
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

In the MCP server (`ng mcp`), `createRootRestrictedHost` only checked `effectiveCwd` before calling `executeNgCommand` / `startNgProcess`. Option flags forwarded from `run_target` via `serializeOptions` (such as `--output-path`, `--out-file`, `--output-file`, `--ts-config`, `--runner-config`, `--karma-config`, etc.) were passed directly to the spawned `ng` command without verifying that their paths remained within the allowed MCP roots.

For example, invoking `run_target` with `{"target": "build", "options": {"output-path": "/path/outside/root"}}` allowed the spawned builder to escape the root-restricted boundary, recursively clean the target directory via `deleteOutputDir` (since `deleteOutputDir` only rejects exact equality with the workspace root), and write build outputs outside allowed MCP roots.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

- **`createRootRestrictedHost` (`packages/angular/cli/src/commands/mcp/host.ts`)**:
  - Validates path-bearing, glob-based, and output-directory CLI flags passed to `executeNgCommand` and `startNgProcess` against the active allowed MCP roots (supporting both `--flag=value` and separate `--flag value` forms, camelCase/kebab-case/snake_case keys, dot-notation, negation forms with `=`, `--runner-args`, and passthrough args after `--`).
  - Rejects output directory flags (`--output-path`, `--output-dir`, etc.) when the resolved target is outside allowed roots **or** is equal to / an ancestor of the effective workspace directory or any allowed root.
  - Validates compound relative output flags (`--out-file`, `--resources-output-path`) against both `cwd` and any supplied output directory, regardless of argument order.
  - Leaves non-filesystem flags intact (e.g., `--base-href`, `--deploy-url`, `--serve-path`, `--route`, `--routes`, `--filter`, `--delete-output-path`, `--output-hashing`, `--output-mode`, and boolean values for union options such as `index`, `server`, `serviceWorker`, and `runnerConfig`).
  - Hardens real-path resolution in `createRootRestrictedHost` to follow dangling symlinks, handle intermediate symlinks before `..` segments, and check exact path separator boundaries (`..` directory prefixes such as `..hidden.txt` inside a root are allowed).
- **`serializeOptions` (`packages/angular/cli/src/commands/mcp/tools/run-target/options-serializer.ts`)**:
  - Tightens option key validation to require a leading alphanumeric character (`^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-_]*$`).
  - Rejects null bytes (`\0`) in string option values.
  - Normalizes `excludeKeys` comparison so case/separator variants cannot bypass excluded keys (e.g., `watch`).
- **`run_target` strategies (`build-target-strategy.ts`, `generic-target-strategy.ts`, `unit-test-strategy.ts`)**:
  - Re-throws non-`CommandError` exceptions (such as root access-denied errors from `createRootRestrictedHost`) instead of catching them as failed command execution logs.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

`deleteOutputDir` in `@angular/build` was intentionally left unchanged so direct `ng build` CLI invocations with explicit external absolute output paths (e.g. `/tmp/...`) continue to work as expected; confinement is enforced at the MCP host boundary.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/cli): validate path options against MCP roots in host execution" (#34773)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): resolve installed @angular/core version in list_projects MCP tool
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The `list_projects` MCP tool works out `frameworkVersion` by walking up from the workspace directory to the first `package.json` that declares `@angular/core`, then passing the declared value to `semver.minVersion`. If the declared value isn't a semver range, `semver.minVersion` throws. That happens with pnpm/yarn catalogs (`catalog:`, `catalog:angular`), `workspace:*` and `npm:` aliases. The tool then reports a versioning error for the workspace (e.g. `Invalid comparator: catalog:`) and leaves `frameworkVersion` unset.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

The version now comes from the installed `@angular/core/package.json`, resolved with `createRequire` the same way the `get_best_practices` tool does it. How the dependency is declared no longer matters.

- Resolution starts from the workspace's `angular.json` file rather than its directory. `createRequire` searches from the parent directory of the path it's given, so starting from the directory would skip the `node_modules` of nested workspaces such as `apps/web`.
- If `@angular/core` isn't installed or its version can't be read, `frameworkVersion` is left unset and no error is reported.
- The upward `package.json` search and its cache are removed.
- The output schema is unchanged.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Issues.Title: fix(@ngtools/webpack): elide const enum imports when rewriting an import declaration
Issues.Body:
## How I found it

I started from #34760 and checked it against the code. In `elide_imports.ts`, once a declaration has to be rewritten because a value specifier is unused (here a class used only as a constructor parameter type), the remaining specifiers are no longer left to TypeScript's own elision. `isValueAlias` treated the const enum as a runtime value, and because its property access counts as a use, the specifier was kept in the rewritten import. With default options the const enum is inlined and the module has no such export, so webpack reports `export 'Period' (imported as 'Period') was not found`.

## Where this can show up in practice

- An `@ngtools/webpack` / `@angular-devkit/build-angular:browser` build where a component or service imports a const enum together with a class that is only used as a type (for example a DI constructor parameter), as in the repro in #34760.
- Shared constants modules that export a `const enum` next to injectable services are a common layout, so more projects on the webpack builder may hit this. This is my estimate; the issue's repro is the only report I know of.

## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

When an import declaration is rewritten, a const enum specifier whose references are inlined is still kept, so the emitted import names an export that does not exist at runtime and the webpack build fails.

Issue Number: Closes #34760

## What is the new behavior?

`isValueAlias` now treats an alias that resolves to a const enum as a non-value alias, unless `preserveConstEnums`, `isolatedModules` or `verbatimModuleSyntax` keeps const enum references (the same options TypeScript itself checks). The specifier is then dropped like a type-only one.

New test in `elide_imports_spec.ts` (`emitDecoratorMetadata` is false): a declaration that imports a const enum and a type-only class, where the class specifier is removed. The expected output has no import and the inlined value `1 /* MixedEnum.A */`.

## Testing

- I could not run the bazel target on the machine I used (macOS). Instead I ran `elide_imports_spec.ts` with jasmine and TypeScript 6.0.3 together with copies of `elide_imports.ts` and `spec_helpers.ts`:
  - without the fix, the new test fails (the output still contains `import { MixedEnum } from './mixed'`) and the other 38 pass;
  - with the fix, all 39 pass.
- As a reference I compared plain `tsc` emit for the same source with the transformer output:
  - with default options both drop the import;
  - with `isolatedModules` both keep it and the reference is not inlined;
  - with `preserveConstEnums` alone `tsc` drops the import and the transformer keeps it. The enum object is emitted in that mode, so the import resolves.
- End to end, I used the repro project from #34760 (Angular 22.2.6, `@ngtools/webpack` 22.2.7). `ng build` fails with the error above. After applying the same change to the installed `elide_imports.js`, the build succeeds and the bundle contains `"month" /* Period.Month */`.
- `prettier --check` passes on both files. CI here is the real check for the bazel target.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@ngtools/webpack): elide const enum imports when rewriting an import declaration" (#34771)

Issues.Title: ng add @angular/ssr fails with TypeError when an NgModule in the app module file has no bootstrap array
Issues.Body:
### Command

add

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

I think before the server schematic started inferring the app component name (commit ea1143dd, April 2025). I have not run an older release to confirm.

### Description

`ng add @angular/ssr` (and `ng generate server`) crashes on an NgModule-based app when one of the `@NgModule` decorators in the file that `main.ts` bootstraps has no `bootstrap` array. The cases I hit:

1. The root module uses `ngDoBootstrap()` instead of `bootstrap: [...]` (Angular Elements apps, AngularJS hybrid apps that bootstrap through `UpgradeModule`).
2. The file declares another `@NgModule` without `bootstrap` (for example a small shared module) before the root module.

In `packages/schematics/angular/utility/standalone/app_component.ts`, `resolveNgModuleBasedData` loops over the module's `@NgModule` decorators and does:

```ts
const bootstrapProp = getMetadataField(node, 'bootstrap').find(...);
const componentIdentifier = (bootstrapProp?.initializer as ts.ArrayLiteralExpression)
  .elements[0] as ts.Identifier | undefined;
```

When `bootstrapProp` is `undefined`, the optional chain stops at `initializer` and `.elements` is read from `undefined`. The function is meant to return `null` in that case: the caller in `server/index.ts` already falls back to `App` / `AppModule` when nothing is found. So the schematic stops with a TypeError instead of using the fallback (case 1) or the right module (case 2).

### Minimal Reproduction

1. `ng new demo --no-standalone`
2. In `src/app/app-module.ts`, remove `bootstrap: [App]` and add `ngDoBootstrap() {}` to `AppModule`.
3. `ng add @angular/ssr`

Or, for case 2, keep `bootstrap: [App]` and put this above `AppModule` in the same file:

```ts
@NgModule({ exports: [] })
export class SharedModule {}
```

I reproduced this with `SchematicTestRunner` against `@schematics/angular` 22.3.0 (workspace -> `application --standalone=false` -> edit the module -> `server` and `ssr` schematics). Both schematics throw for case 1, and `server` throws for case 2. The unmodified app works.

### Exception or Error

```text
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'elements')
    at resolveNgModuleBasedData (node_modules/@schematics/angular/utility/standalone/app_component.js:65:14)
```

### Your Environment

```text
@schematics/angular 22.3.0
@angular-devkit/schematics 22.3.0
Node.js 22.23.5
```

### Anything else relevant?

Skipping decorators that have no `bootstrap` field (`continue`, like the `ts.isObjectLiteralExpression` check just above it) is enough to fix both cases: case 2 then finds `AppModule`, and case 1 falls through to the existing fallback. I have a patch with two tests in `server/index_spec.ts` and can open a PR.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "ng add @angular/ssr fails with TypeError when an NgModule in the app module file has no bootstrap array" (#34761)

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): skip NgModules without bootstrap when resolving the app component
Issues.Body:
## How I found it

A lint pass (oxlint `no-unsafe-optional-chaining`) flagged the server schematic's module lookup in `utility/standalone/app_component.ts`, and I read the code to check it. The optional chain in `(bootstrapProp?.initializer as ts.ArrayLiteralExpression).elements[0]` stops at `initializer`, so `.elements` is read from `undefined` whenever `find` returns nothing. I then reproduced it with `SchematicTestRunner` against `@schematics/angular` 22.3.0 (details in #34761).

## Where this can show up in practice

- An Angular Elements app, or an AngularJS hybrid app, whose root module uses `ngDoBootstrap()` and has no `bootstrap` array: `ng add @angular/ssr` stops with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'elements')`.
- A module file that declares a small shared or routing `@NgModule` above the root module: the first decorator has no `bootstrap`, so the lookup throws before it reaches `AppModule`.
- A root module with `bootstrap: []` left over from a refactor.

This is my estimate; I have not seen a field report.

## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

`resolveNgModuleBasedData` throws when an `@NgModule` decorator in the bootstrapped module's file has no usable `bootstrap` array, so the `server` and `ssr` schematics fail instead of using the next module or the existing `App` / `AppModule` fallback in `server/index.ts`.

Issue Number: Closes #34761

## What is the new behavior?

Decorators without a `bootstrap` array are skipped with `continue`, like the `ts.isObjectLiteralExpression` check just above. If no module has one, the function returns `null` and the caller's fallback applies.

Two tests in `server/index_spec.ts` (non standalone application):

- a shared `@NgModule` without `bootstrap` declared before the root module: the root module's component is still used;
- a root module that uses `ngDoBootstrap()`: the schematic completes and writes `app.module.server.ts`.

## Testing

- I could not run `bazel test //packages/schematics/angular:test` on the machine I used (linux-arm64; `rules_browsers` has no chromium for that platform, so analysis fails).
- Instead I transpiled the changed `server/index_spec.ts` and `app_component.ts` with the repo's TypeScript and ran the spec with jasmine against the published `@schematics/angular` 22.3.0:
  - without the fix, the two new tests fail with the TypeError above and the other 21 pass;
  - with the fix, all 23 pass. The unchanged `ssr/index_spec.ts` (10 specs) also passes with the fix.
- `prettier --check` passes on both files.
- CI here is the real check for the bazel target.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): destroy the platform of an aborted request once it…
Issues.Body:
… is stable

Aborting a request destroyed the platform while an app initializer or an `HttpClient` request was still pending, which could end the server process. The platform is now destroyed once the application is stable, or after 10 seconds.

Fixes #34754

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): guard aborted requests across rendering and serialization
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

When a request is aborted during SSR rendering:
- `AngularServerApp.handleRendering()` can still perform asset reads, run `html:transform:pre` hooks, invoke `renderAngular()`, or run Beasties `inlineCriticalCss()` after `request.signal` has already aborted.
- `renderAngular()` does not check `moduleRef.injector.destroyed`, `applicationRef.destroyed`, `platformRef.destroyed` (post-`whenStable`), or `destroyPromise` consistently across bootstrap, stability, and `content()`, only clears `renderTimeoutId` on the first `destroy()` call, detaches abort listeners two microtasks after `content()` settles, and can leave `asyncDestroyPlatform()` unresolved if `platformRef.destroy()` throws.

Companion framework fix: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/72139
Related issue: #34754

## What is the new behavior?

- Short-circuit `AngularServerApp.handleRendering()` on `request.signal.aborted` before asset reads, `html:transform:pre` hooks, `renderAngular()`, redirect response creation, and critical CSS inlining, and uniformly await `result.destroy()` when aborting inside the response `ReadableStream`.
- Keep immediate platform destruction on abort in `renderAngular()` (relying on the framework teardown fixes in https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/72139 instead of deferring destruction or adding fallback timeouts).
- Guard `moduleRef.injector.destroyed`, `applicationRef.destroyed`, `platformRef.destroyed`, and `destroyPromise` consistently across `renderAngular()` and `content()`, clear `renderTimeoutId` on every `destroy()` call, detach abort listeners before settling `content()`, and wrap `platformRef.destroy()` in `try`/`finally` inside `asyncDestroyPlatform()`.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] No

Issues.Body:

This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Adoption](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Passing](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm/npm/pnpm)) | [`12.18.0` → `12.21.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/12.18.0/12.21.0) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/12.21.0?slim=true) | ![adoption](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/adoption/npm/pnpm/12.21.0?slim=true) | ![passing](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/compatibility/npm/pnpm/12.18.0/12.21.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/12.18.0/12.21.0?slim=true) | --- - [ ] If you want to rebase/retry this PR, check this box --- ### Release Notes
pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v12.21.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.21.0): pnpm 12.21 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.20.0...v12.21.0) pnpm 12.21.0 lets `pnpm store add` prepare tarball and git dependencies for offline installs. It also makes repeated installs keep their peer dependency choices and fixes several `lockfile.format: v13`, `nodeLinker: hoisted`, and `pnpm deploy` failures. If a pnpr server refuses a setting, pnpm now resolves locally. ##### Minor Changes - `pnpm store add` run in a project now prepares downloaded tarballs for every lockfile entry that pins them. Besides registry packages, `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` can then install dependencies on a tarball URL and dependencies on a git host such as GitHub whose lockfile entry records an `integrity`. ##### Patch Changes ##### Installs that failed - pnpm now reads a lockfile with a mapping key longer than 1,024 characters written as `'key':`, without the `? ` marker. Before, `pnpm install` and other commands failed on such a lockfile with `ERR_PNPM_BROKEN_LOCKFILE`. - With `lockfile.format: v13`, `pnpm install` no longer fails to create or rewrite the lockfile when a package declares many of its dependencies as peers. - Fixed `pnpm deploy` failing with `lockfile.format: v13` when injected workspace packages have hashed peer bindings. - Frozen installs with v13 lockfiles now accept valid peer dependencies of injected workspace packages that use catalogs. - Fixed injected workspace packages that depend on themselves linking to a nonexistent directory. - `pnpm install` with `frozenStore` enabled no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_FROZEN_STORE_NEEDS_BUILD` when `nodeLinker` is `hoisted`. `pnpm fetch` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` no longer populates global virtual store links or modifies linked agent skills, and it preserves an existing hoisted `node_modules` directory [#​18037](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18037). - A `requirements.txt` beside a `pyproject.toml` that declares `[tool.uv.workspace]` without a `[project]` table no longer makes that directory a Python project. `pnpm install` stopped there with an error when the directory had a `.venv` that pnpm did not create [#​18023](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18023). ##### Peer dependencies - Repeated installs no longer change the peer dependency providers that the previous install chose. This covers adding, updating, or removing a dependency, projects that use different ranges of one dependency, dependency cycles, and injected dependencies with `autoInstallPeers: false` [pnpm/tasks#221](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/221). An unchanged install keeps a valid locked peer provider even when a direct dependency provides another compatible version. Explicit `pnpm add` and `pnpm update` requests take precedence over it. - Workspace projects that select different versions of a peer provider no longer share one copy of the package that depends on it. This affected peers reached through an aliased dependency or a peer dependency cycle. - A removed dependency no longer comes back as a peer provider. Before, a direct dependency removed with `autoInstallPeers: false` could be restored from an old peer resolution, and a removed one could still supply its old peer context. - With `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `autoInstallPeers: false`, `pnpm install` no longer creates duplicate copies of a package whose resolved peers are identical. A package also no longer loads a copy of its dependency that was resolved with different peer versions [#​18003](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18003). - `pnpm deploy` now binds optional peers declared only in `peerDependenciesMeta` for linked workspace packages. The deployed manifest and lockfile also retain these peers when filtering dependency groups. ##### Running scripts - Scripts now stop when pnpm's process group is killed while they are starting. - Bin shims in the global virtual store no longer include the hoisted modules directory of the project that installed them [#​18035](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18035). - `pnpm pipeline` now rebuilds local packages and reruns build scripts after it restores a shared Cargo build cache with Cargo 1.100 or newer. Before, a worktree could reuse build-script output from the worktree that created the cache. ##### pnpr - If the pnpr server refuses a setting the install uses, or cannot return the lockfile format pnpm reads, `pnpm install` and `pnpm update` print a warning and resolve locally. Cargo and Python resolution also fall back to resolving locally. pnpm now rejects a pnpr resolution of npm dependencies that does not name its lockfile format. - `pnpm install` with `pnprServer` now limits the size of the server's resolve and lockfile verification responses. An oversized response ends the request with an error. - pnpm now displays pnpr error codes and reasons when remote requests fail. ##### Other commands and settings - `pnpm setup` and the install script now support PowerShell as the login shell on Linux and macOS. They add `PNPM_HOME` to `PATH` in `profile.ps1` under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/powershell` or `~/.config/powershell` [#​18026](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/18026). - A `lockfileDir` setting that points at the default lockfile directory now installs the same way as leaving it unset [pnpm/tasks#275](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/275). ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.20.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.20.0): pnpm 12.20 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.19.0...v12.20.0) pnpm 12.20.0 records the specifiers of local directory dependencies in the experimental v13 lockfile and fixes several `nodeLinker: hoisted`, peer dependency, and `overrides` bugs. The bundled `node-gyp` no longer ships the undici version that security scanners flag. Remote resolution and shared build caches no longer work with pnpr 0.1.0-alpha.19 or older. ##### Minor Changes - With `lockfile.format: v13`, `pnpm install` records the dependency specifiers of local directory packages. Frozen installs reject changed specifiers even when the locked versions still satisfy them. ##### Patch Changes ##### Upgrading and security - Remote resolution, shared build caches, and release notes no longer work with pnpr 0.1.0-alpha.19 or older. pnpm now reads the capabilities a pnpr server advertises under `pnpr.protocols`. Installs fail when the server does not confirm the requested resolution and verification policies. - The `node-gyp` bundled with pnpm no longer ships undici 6, which security scanners flag for CVE-2026-84947. On Node.js 26, `node-gyp` downloads through a proxy or with a custom CA file no longer crash with "invalid onError method" [#​17941](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17941). ##### Resolving dependencies - Version-selector `overrides` entries such as `"ms@^2.0.0": "2.1.1"` now apply to dependencies declared with the `catalog:` protocol when the catalog entry's range matches the selector [#​17922](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17922). - A root `overrides` entry that points a package at a `workspace:` path, such as `workspace:./packages/foo`, now also applies when a registry package depends on that package [pnpm/tasks#270](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/270). - Git dependencies now accept npm's `::` separator between fragment parameters, such as `github:owner/repo#v1.0.0::path:packages/foo`. Before, pnpm read the whole fragment as a branch name and failed to resolve it [#​17827](https://redirect.github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/17827). - `pnpm dedupe` now keeps a locked runtime version, from `devEngines.runtime` or from a dependency's `engines.runtime`, when the declared range still admits it. `pnpm dedupe --check` no longer fails each time a newer Node.js release in the range comes out [#​17984](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17984). - With `autoInstallPeersFromHighestMatch`, conflicting non-semver peer dependencies now remain missing, and identical non-semver peer specifiers are preserved. Preferred registry versions no longer replace local paths or protocol-prefixed specifiers when pnpm installs missing peers [pnpm/tasks#272](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/272). ##### Hoisted node linker - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, a package now keeps its nested copy of a dependency that it resolved at a version other than the top-level one, including a peer dependency its parent supplies. Before, pnpm could remove that copy as a duplicate or give the top-level slot to a peer variant found deeper in the graph. The package then loaded the top-level version. ##### Lockfile and peer dependency graphs - Fixed `pnpm install` keeping stale peer bindings after dependency changes. Required dependencies no longer remain marked optional when another workspace project removes a shared package [pnpm/tasks#221](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/221). - Repeated installs now keep the same dependency links when packages form cycles with several peer dependency variants [pnpm/tasks#221](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/221). - Fixed writing `lockfile.format: v13` for dependency cycles with missing, optional, or transitive peers. Frozen installs also accept unchanged injected packages whose peers use catalogs. With `--no-optional`, frozen installs reject required catalog children recorded only as optional dependencies [pnpm/tasks#221](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/221). - `pnpm deploy` preserves an injected workspace package's resolved dependencies when they differ from the workspace project's own dependencies. This also applies to packages with `publishConfig.directory` [pnpm/tasks#221](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/221). ##### Running scripts and runtimes - Scripts that pnpm runs in a process group of their own are now ended when pnpm is killed right after starting them. A parallel run that was killed before pnpm registered its scripts left all of them running. - When a command name matches no script and pnpm falls back to running it as a command, the install that runs before scripts now runs once. Its errors and warnings print once [#​17977](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17977). - Failed downloads by project-aware global runtime commands now explain which configuration applies. Node.js failures also list the global mirror settings and environment variables to check. ##### Other commands and settings - Fixed `pnpm` occasionally crashing on the first HTTPS request, mostly on Windows virtual machines under load. pnpm now seeds TLS randomness from the operating system's random number generator [pnpm/tasks#239](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/239). - Fixed `pnpm deprecate`, `pnpm undeprecate`, and `pnpm unpublish` failing with revision conflicts when a registry cache serves stale package metadata. - `pnpm sbom` now reports malformed workspace manifests. Before, it omitted their packages [pnpm/tasks#59](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/59). - Fixed `pnpm store status` reporting approved builds of git dependencies as modified when the store contains legacy build metadata. - pnpm now recognizes Capawesome Cloud and RWX as CI environments. ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.19.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.19.0): pnpm 12.19 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.18.0...v12.19.0) pnpm 12.19.0 adds `pnpm fund`, lets the `loaded` node linker handle packages that need a build, and adds the `projectScopedOptionalPeers` setting and an experimental JSON lockfile format. It also includes a security fix: an offline install error no longer prints registry credentials. pnpm now checks the `engines` and platform fields of every workspace project, and many hoisted-linker and frozen-lockfile bugs are fixed. ##### Minor Changes - Added `pnpm fund`, which lists the funding URLs declared by the installed dependencies in the same tree `npm fund` prints. Use `--json` for the `npm fund --json` report and `--recursive` or `--filter` to report on workspace projects. `pnpm fund ` opens the funding URL of an installed package, and `--which` picks one when it lists several [#​7354](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7354). - With `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, packages that need a build no longer have to be listed in `nodeLinker.excluded`. A package with a matching side-effects cache entry loads from the store. If side-effects cache reads and writes are enabled, pnpm builds an approved package once, saves the result to the side-effects cache, and then loads it from the store. This includes a build that changes no files in its package, so its script does not run again in other projects that use the same store. List a package in `sideEffectsCache.exclude` if its build must run in every project, such as a git hook installer. pnpm materializes other cache misses, packages with native `.node` addons, and their dependencies automatically. pnpm also scans JavaScript sources for filesystem imports and for `__dirname` or `import.meta`, and materializes matching packages. The scan does not detect computed imports. List such packages in `nodeLinker.excluded`. - Added the `projectScopedOptionalPeers` setting. When it is `true`, a project gets a missing optional peer dependency only if the project's own dependencies install a version of it. Another workspace project's dependencies, such as its `devDependencies`, no longer supply one. `dedupePeerDependents` keeps deduplicating everything else [#​16666](https://redirect.github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/16666). - Added the experimental `lockfile.format: v13` setting. With it, pnpm writes `pnpm-lock.yaml` in a JSON-like syntax, indented with tabs, with a trailing comma after every entry. The file is still valid YAML. The file has one `packages` entry per package version in place of the `packages` and `snapshots` sections, and each entry records the versions of its peer dependencies as its properties. Updating a peer dependency then changes only the lines that record its version. pnpm reads lockfiles in both formats whatever the setting is. - `pnpm store add` now accepts directories of tarballs, such as `pnpm store add ./tarballs`, and adds every `.tgz`, `.tar.gz`, and `.tar` file inside them recursively. `pnpm store add` is now faster when it adds many packages or local tarballs [#​17875](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17875). - With `supportedArchitectures` set, `pnpm install` and `pnpm fetch` also store, without linking them, the dependencies of the archives kept for the other listed platforms. A platform added to the setting gets its archives and their dependencies on the next install. Optional dependencies a listed platform cannot run are not stored, and one that fails to download is skipped. Dependencies from git repositories are not stored for other platforms. - When `supportedArchitectures` names exactly one platform and not `current`, pnpm links that platform's variant of a package published with platform variants, together with that variant's dependencies. This holds for the list form and for the `os`, `cpu`, and `libc` form. A variant whose floor or ABI the listed platform does not state is not linked for it: pnpm links another variant that fits, or the version's own archive. Changing the setting, or the platform of the host, such as a `node_modules` mounted into a musl container or a Node.js with another ABI, relinks the package on the next install, even from a frozen lockfile. - pnpm now provides a prebuilt binary for NetBSD 10 on x64 [#​17803](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17803). ##### Patch Changes ##### Security - The error for a tarball that is missing from the store in offline mode no longer prints the credentials or token in the tarball URL. ##### Installs that failed or hung - `pnpm install`, `pnpm ci`, and `pnpm install-test` outside a workspace now fail with `ERR_PNPM_NO_PKG_MANIFEST` when the directory has no `package.json`, `package.json5`, or `package.yaml`. They no longer create a `package.json`, a lockfile, and `node_modules` there [#​17727](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17727). - Fixed `pnpm install` hanging when a concurrent tarball download or manifest read is cancelled while other tasks are waiting on the same archive. - Running a global command such as `node` in a project that pins its version no longer hangs while pnpm installs that version. The hang kept starting new processes until the machine ran out of memory. - A global command such as `node` now runs the version a project pins when `PNPM_CONFIG_LOCKFILE_DIR`, `PNPM_CONFIG_VIRTUAL_STORE_ONLY`, or `PNPM_CONFIG_SYMLINK` is set in the environment. Before, the dispatch failed with "the installed node executable is not under" the store. - `pnpm install` now fetches fresh metadata for a package when a version allowed by `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` is missing from the cached metadata. Before, it could fail with `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION` without contacting the registry [#​17723](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17723). - A `${VAR}` placeholder in a registry URL in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the project `.npmrc` now fails the command. pnpm does not expand environment variables in these files. Before, pnpm ignored such a URL and resolved packages from another registry, such as npmjs.org. pnpm now warns when it ignores a placeholder in a proxy, `pnprServer`, or `userAgent` setting in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` [#​17762](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17762). - Fixed local package installs failing while a workspace lockfile is being written. - `pnpm self-update` and switching to the `packageManager` version now work behind a proxy that ends a response by closing the TLS connection without a `close_notify` alert. The registry signature check failed there with `ERR_PNPM_PNPM_ENGINE_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIABLE` [#​17763](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17763). - A package tarball that keeps failing to download now fails the install after `fetchRetries` retries. pnpm used to download it again with a second full set of retries, which doubled the wait. The error now names the actual download failure. - When the native binary of the pnpm version a project pins fails to download, pnpm now reports the download error. It used to report only that no native binary was found for the host. - POSIX bin shims and the `pnpm`, `pn`, `pnpx`, and `pnx` launchers now run inside a Nix build on macOS with the sandbox enabled. Installing again replaces the shims already in `node_modules` [#​17750](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17750). - Fixed pnpm leaving process pipes open after it exits on macOS [pnpm/tasks#229](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/229). ##### Engines and platform checks - `pnpm install`, `pnpm add`, `pnpm update`, and `pnpm remove` now check the `engines`, `os`, `cpu`, and `libc` fields of every workspace project, including the workspace root. `pnpm run -r` and `pnpm exec -r` check them before running anything. An incompatible `engines.pnpm` fails the command. An incompatible `engines.node` prints a warning, or fails the command with `engineStrict` enabled. An unsupported platform prints a warning. A project that downloads its own Node.js through `devEngines.runtime` is checked against that Node.js [#​17751](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17751) [pnpm/tasks#281](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/281) [pnpm/tasks#299](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/299). - Fixed missing warnings when a required dependency does not support the current Node.js version. - An optional dependency that declares no `os`, `cpu`, or `libc` field is no longer skipped because its name contains only an operating system word, such as `get-windows` on macOS. pnpm now infers its platform from the name only when the name also has a cpu or libc token, such as `-win32-x64` [#​17774](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17774). ##### Peer dependencies - With `dedupePeerDependents: false`, a missing optional peer is no longer resolved from a version that only another workspace project depends on. The workspace root's dependencies still count if `resolvePeersFromWorkspaceRoot` is `true`. Before, a tool in one project's `devDependencies`, such as `webpack-cli`, could become an optional peer of another project's production dependencies [#​16666](https://redirect.github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/16666). - `pnpm install` no longer gives a project an optional peer dependency that it skipped because a required peer would conflict with the project's dependencies. Before, `dedupePeerDependents` merged the project's copy of the package that declares the peer with another project's copy that resolves it [#​17781](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17781). - `pnpm install` no longer fills in a missing optional peer dependency if a required peer it brings in conflicts with a version the project depends on. Before, such a peer was installed along with it and reported as unmet [#​17718](https://redirect.github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/17718). - `pnpm install --filter` in a sparse checkout now counts the dependencies of workspace projects that are missing from disk when it resolves peer dependencies and marks packages as optional. The lockfile it writes no longer differs from a full checkout in those entries [#​17791](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17791). ##### Frozen lockfile and workspace links - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now succeeds when a workspace project recorded in `pnpm-lock.yaml` has an empty directory, such as a git submodule that was not checked out [#​17712](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17712). - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` when a workspace package linked through a plain semver range, such as `^7.9.5`, has changed to a version outside that range [#​17806](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17806). - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now accept a `workspace:` dependency on a project whose version is not valid semver, such as `workspace:1` on a project at version `1`. Before, they reported the lockfile that `pnpm install` had just written as out of date. - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts a lockfile when an injected workspace package declares a `file:` or `link:` dependency with backslashes, such as `file:..\vendor`, or with a slash after the protocol, such as `file:/./vendor`. Before, the install reported the lockfile as out of date right after `pnpm install` had written it [#​17720](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17720). - When a package injected through a path, such as `file:../lib` or `../lib`, gives one of its dependencies a `catalog:` specifier, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now reports the lockfile as outdated. For a bare path such as `../lib`, `pnpm install` now also fails the way a fresh resolution does. Before, these installs accepted the existing lockfile [#​17722](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17722). - Dependencies declared as `workspace:` entries in catalogs now remain in the lockfile when `excludeLinksFromLockfile` is enabled. Frozen installs can restore these links after `node_modules` is removed [pnpm/tasks#260](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/260). - With `dedupeDirectDeps`, `pnpm install` now compares `link:` dependencies by the directory they point at. A project's `link:` dependency is removed when the workspace root links the same directory under a different path. It is kept when the root's `link:` dependency has the same text but points at another directory. pnpm reports a dependency the root provides as removed only once, when it removes the project's link. The summary shows the package version of a removed `link:` dependency [pnpm/tasks#293](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/293). ##### Hoisted node linker and custom modulesDir - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, a package that runs a lifecycle script or has a patch is now cloned or copied into `node_modules`, as with the isolated linker. A build that rewrites one of its files no longer changes the store copy shared with other projects. - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, pnpm no longer deletes a directory outside `node_modules` when it removes a package whose scope directory is a symlink. - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, `pnpm install --filter` in a sparse checkout now drops previously installed workspace projects that are missing from disk from the hoisted `node_modules` tree. It no longer recreates `node_modules` inside a missing project's directory. Packages that only the missing project used are also removed from the root `node_modules`. - With `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `dedupeDirectDeps`, `pnpm install` now removes a project's `link:` dependency that the workspace root provides, and reports each `link:` dependency it removes. Removing the last scoped `link:` dependency of a scope also removes the empty `@scope` directory. - With `nodeLinker: hoisted` and a custom `modulesDir`, pnpm now installs a workspace project's dependencies that cannot be hoisted to the root into the project's `modulesDir`. The next install that relinks the project removes the copies that earlier installs left in its `node_modules`. A later install restores the project's `modulesDir` when it was removed. Package directories that pnpm did not install are now also moved to `.ignored` in a custom `modulesDir`. - Fixed installs in a workspace whose `modulesDir` is an absolute path, including one that goes through a symlink such as `/tmp` on macOS, or a path that starts with `..`. Dependencies of workspace projects no longer end up outside the workspace, and the root project's dependencies, `link:` dependencies, and commands are linked into the configured directory. `pnpm bin`, `pnpm root`, `pnpm run`, `pnpm exec`, and `pnpm version` now use that directory too [pnpm/tasks#285](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/285). ##### Store and builds - Concurrent installs into a global virtual store no longer wait on each other. A package that needs a build is built in a private directory and moved into the store once its build has finished, so another project never links a half-built package. An install with `--ignore-scripts` links the packages it does not build from their own store directories, and `pnpm store prune` removes the build directories of installs that were interrupted [#​15568](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15568). - Packages that an older pnpm version added to the store now run their install scripts. Before, pnpm could skip those scripts and hardlink the package's files to the store. - `pnpm install` now keeps patches to bundled dependencies when it restores a package from the side-effects cache, including files a patch adds [#​17734](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17734). - Local installs on macOS now keep cached clones separate from the global virtual store. `pnpm store prune` removes this cache, so unused cached packages no longer accumulate [#​17907](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17907). - `pnpm store prune` now stops if a dependency link cannot be read. This keeps installed packages from being removed after an incomplete scan. - A repeat `pnpm install` now runs a full install when the `runtimeOnFail` setting changes. Before, it printed "Already up to date" and did not install the runtime a project declares in `devEngines.runtime` [pnpm/tasks#303](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/303). - The sync of an injected workspace dependency now copies a file whose source has reached the filesystem's limit on hard links. `pnpm patch-commit` now copies a file into its scratch directory when the filesystem refuses to hard link it, unless the path is missing or already occupied [pnpm/tasks#283](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/283). ##### Speed - `pnpm install` is faster when it clones files from the store, which it does by default on macOS. On a Mac with endpoint security software, a cold install of a project with about 1,350 packages took 29% less time [pnpm/tasks#280](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/280). - `pnpm install` unpacks packages that contain many files faster. Unpacking `typescript` took 30% less time in our measurements [pnpm/tasks#288](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/288). - Resolving against a registry that sends `Cache-Control: no-cache`, such as Azure Artifacts, is fast again when the lockfile already decides the version. pnpm reads the cached metadata for a pinned version, or for a range the lockfile version is proven to win, without a registry request [#​17758](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17758). - POSIX bin shims start fewer processes. Running a dependency's bin through its shim from Git Bash on Windows starts 7 processes where it started 15. Installing again replaces the shims already in `node_modules`. ##### Windows - pnpm now installs dependencies and runs lifecycle scripts from projects on mapped Windows network drives. When a network share refuses the links in `node_modules`, the error now suggests setting `nodeLinker: hoisted` or moving the project to a local drive [#​17747](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17747). - `packageImportMethod: auto` now tries hardlinking before cloning, as it does on Linux. Installs from a warm store on a Dev Drive are faster. An install no longer fails when the store refuses a hardlink with an access-denied error, and pnpm tries cloning or copying the file next [#​17809](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17809). - `pnpm run` and `pnpm setup` no longer clear the visible terminal when a project path contains non-ASCII characters. - A failed attempt to create a directory junction in `node_modules` no longer leaves a `.pnpm-junction-*` directory behind. - `pnpm` starts faster. It loads system libraries such as `user32.dll` and `shell32.dll` the first time a command uses them, so `pnpm --version` loads 11 libraries where it loaded 25. ##### pnpm deploy - `pnpm deploy` now runs the build scripts of a workspace project that it installs as a `file:` dependency, without a machine-specific `allowBuilds` key. An `allowBuilds` entry that denies the project still applies [#​17740](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17740). - `pnpm deploy` no longer fails when the deployed project depends on a workspace package that sets `publishConfig.directory`. pnpm installs that package from its publish directory and runs its build scripts [#​17771](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17771). - `pnpm deploy` without a shared workspace lockfile now resolves a relative `workspace:` path, such as `workspace:../lib`, from the source project's directory. It used to be resolved from the deploy target and fail [#​17804](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17804). - `pnpm deploy --offline --trust-lockfile` now reuses dependencies pinned in the source lockfile from a populated store when registry metadata is unavailable. This works with per-project lockfiles, `--legacy`, and npm aliases [#​17888](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17888). ##### Other commands and settings - `pnpm dist-tag` and `pnpm unpublish` now offer browser-based authentication when the account's two-factor authentication uses a security key. Before, they asked for a one-time password in that case [#​17832](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17832). - `pnpm publish` with provenance now downloads Sigstore's current signing configuration before signing. A failed or slow download is retried with the same retry policy and deadline as the signing requests. - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now apply the first rule of a `.npmignore` or `.gitignore` that starts with a UTF-8 BOM. - `pnpm outdated` now checks dependencies when the project has no lockfile, for example with `lockfile: false`. The `Current` column shows the installed version, or the lowest version allowed by the declared range if the dependency is not installed [#​17811](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17811). - `pnpm self-update` now updates the project's `engines.pnpm` range along with its pnpm pin, keeping the `^` or `~` operator [#​17732](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17732). - On Linux and macOS, `pnpm run` no longer sometimes reports a lifecycle failure after `Ctrl+C` interrupts a script. - Config dependencies use the declared registry `serverType` when recording and installing packages [pnpm/tasks#236](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/236). - Relative directory selectors set on `config.filter` or `config.filterProd` by an `updateConfig` hook now resolve from the workspace root even when `--dir` is passed or `pnpm` runs from a subdirectory [#​17906](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17906). - Commands that add settings to `pnpm-workspace.yaml` now fail with an error if the file contains only `null`, and leave the file unchanged. Before, they wrote invalid YAML. - Shell tab-completion now completes directory and file paths for path options such as `-C`, `--dir`, `--prefix`, `--store-dir`, and `--env-file`. Before, options without a fixed list of values offered command names [#​17884](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17884). ##### Platinum Sponsors

### [`v0.8.0`](https://redirect.github.com/bazel-contrib/jq.bzl/releases/tag/v0.8.0)

#### Using Bzlmod with Bazel 6 or greater

1. (Bazel 6 only) Enable with `common --enable_bzlmod` in `.bazelrc`.
2. Add to your `MODULE.bazel` file:

```starlark
bazel_dep(name = "jq.bzl", version = "0.8.0")
```

#### Using WORKSPACE

Paste this snippet into your `WORKSPACE.bazel` file:

```starlark
load("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:http.bzl", "http_archive")
http_archive(
    name = "jq.bzl",
    sha256 = "69963aeaa6ca5f9c1a2810c6e5253c37828c515fb82f39526bccf36f01cd791c",
    strip_prefix = "jq.bzl-0.8.0",
    url = "https://github.com/bazel-contrib/jq.bzl/releases/download/v0.8.0/jq.bzl-v0.8.0.tar.gz",
)
```

Issues.Title: Angular SSR can crash `AngularAppEngine` servers with a single aborted request (22.2.6 regression)
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

22.2.5

### Description


Since `@angular/ssr` 22.2.6, a client that disconnects while a page is still rendering can kill the server process when it runs on `AngularAppEngine`: plain `node:http`, Hono, H3, srvx, Deno or Bun. The Express server from `ng new --ssr` is fine, because `AngularNodeAppEngine` installs process-wide error handlers.

#34568 made `renderAngular()` destroy the platform when `request.signal` aborts:

https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/72f44d79cb577821bbfa849f5bb3b41eee87c2ab/packages/angular/ssr/src/utils/ng.ts#L126-L129

The host still gets the usual `AbortError` and handles it. What kills the process is the work that was still running. The clearest case is an app initializer: once it settles, [`bootstrap()` reads the destroyed injector](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/v22.2.6/packages/core/src/platform/bootstrap.ts#L143-L146), and the internal error handler [rethrows the `NG0205` from a `setTimeout`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/v22.2.6/packages/core/src/error_handler.ts#L155-L160) because the injector is destroyed. Neither the app nor the host's `try/catch` can catch that, so it doesn't matter how the initializer is written:

| Pending when the client disconnects, on `AngularAppEngine` | Process |
| --- | --- |
| `provideAppInitializer` from its [usage notes](https://angular.dev/api/core/provideAppInitializer#usage-notes) | exit 1 |
| the same wrapped in `try/catch` | exit 1 |
| an initializer that only waits on a 100 ms timer | exit 1 |
| `PendingTasks.run()` as the [zoneless guide](https://angular.dev/guide/zoneless#pendingtasks-for-server-side-rendering-ssr) shows it, awaiting an `HttpClient` call | exit 1 |
| `firstValueFrom(http.get(...))` in `async ngOnInit()` (zoneless) | exit 1 |
| `subscribe()`, resolvers, guards, `httpResource`, `resource()` | alive |
| the `try/catch` initializer on 22.2.5, or on `AngularNodeAppEngine` | alive |

The `ngOnInit` row is the other path: `FetchBackend` [completes without a value](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/v22.2.6/packages/common/http/src/fetch.ts#L267-L270) once the app is destroyed, so `firstValueFrom()` rejects with `EmptyError` and nobody holds that promise. `PendingTasks.run()` passes that error to the same internal error handler, so it's rethrown from a `setTimeout` too.

It doesn't take precise timing. Every abort that arrived while the server was waiting on its backend killed it, 310 out of 310 with backends from 1 ms to 1 s, and nginx with its default config passes the abort on. The other pages that were rendering go down too. With Docker's `restart: always`, one aborted request every two seconds left the site serving 312 pages a minute instead of 5,584.

#34568 is right to stop the render, but the platform shouldn't be destroyed while that work is still pending, so the abort stays inside the promise `handle()` returns, the way it did on 22.2.5. `AngularAppEngine` is meant for platforms other than Node.js, so it can't count on `process.on()` handlers like `AngularNodeAppEngine` does.

### Minimal Reproduction


https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/angular-ssr-abort-crash-lab

`ng new --ssr` with `provideHttpClient()`, `RenderMode.Server` on `**`, the SSR guide's non-Node entry on `node:http`, and a component that waits for its data during the render (`api.mjs` answers in 100 ms):

```ts
async ngOnInit() {
  const { name } = await firstValueFrom(
    this.http.get<{ name: string }>('http://127.0.0.1:4400/profile'),
  );
  this.profile.set(name);
}
```

```sh
npm ci && npx ng build
node api.mjs &
node dist/aborted-render-process/server/server.mjs &
sleep 2
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:4000/
curl -sS -m 0.05 http://localhost:4000/
sleep 1
curl -sS http://localhost:4000/
```

```text
200
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 55 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
curl: (7) Failed to connect to localhost:4000 after 0 ms: Could not connect to server
```

The initializer version is in `variants/initializer-trycatch`, and `cd docker && sh variants.sh initializer-trycatch` builds and runs it. The README has the rest.

### Exception or Error

```text
The try/catch initializer, development build:

dist/aborted-render-process/server/main.server.mjs:4818
            throw e;
            ^

RuntimeError: NG0205: Injector has already been destroyed. Find more at https://v22.angular.dev/errors/NG0205
    at assertNotDestroyed (dist/aborted-render-process/server/main.server.mjs:3546:11)
    at R3Injector.get (dist/aborted-render-process/server/main.server.mjs:3303:5)
    at dist/aborted-render-process/server/main.server.mjs:26095:38
    at async renderAngular (dist/aborted-render-process/server/main.server.mjs:43273:24)


The ngOnInit repro, development build:

node:internal/process/promises:394
    triggerUncaughtException(err, true /* fromPromise */);
    ^
Error
    at new EmptyErrorImpl (dist/aborted-render-process/server/main.server.mjs:1783:3)
    at Object.complete (dist/aborted-render-process/server/main.server.mjs:1802:18) {
  message: 'no elements in sequence'
}
```

### Your Environment

```text
@angular/ssr      22.2.7
@angular/core     22.2.6, also 22.3.0
Node.js           24.16.0 on Windows 11, 24.22.3 in Docker
Also tried        Hono 4.13, H3 2.0, srvx 1.0, Deno 2.9.8, Bun 1.4.4, nginx 1.30
```

### Anything else relevant?


I think this is a vulnerability according to the [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/SECURITY.md), which says:

> DoS attacks which waste server resources significantly beyond the cost of the attacker's request may be security issues.

Here a single request crashes the server.

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/tree): avoid searching through a node's set to determine its position
Issues.Body:
`CdkTree._getPositionInSet()` computed a node's `aria-posinset` by searching through its set with `findIndex`. Every `cdk-tree-node` and `mat-tree-node` binds the position and it's re-evaluated during each change detection, so checking a tree took time quadratic in the number of siblings. The issue measured about 2 s per click with 40,000 siblings.

These changes record each node's position when its set is built and look it up instead. They're based on the diff that @TomoyukiAota suggested in the issue, thanks for the detailed report and measurements.

Differences from the suggested diff:
- The positions are stored per set (`Map<K | null, Map<K, number>>`), keyed the same way as `_ariaSets`. The lookup goes through `_parents` like `_getAriaSet()` does, so it reads from the same set as before, even if a key appears in more than one set.
- If a key appears more than once in a set, its first position is kept, which matches `findIndex`.
- All writes to `_ariaSets` go through two helpers that update the positions as well: `_setAriaSet()` (children accessor, flat and nested) and `_appendToAriaSet()` (level accessor). The positions are cleared in `_clearPreviousCache()` together with `_ariaSets`. In `_calculateParents()`, `group.splice(index, 0, node)` always appended, since a set can't hold more nodes than precede the current one, so it's now a plain append.
- A node without a set still gets position 1, and a node missing from its parent's set still gets 0, as before.

Tests added to `src/cdk/tree/tree.spec.ts`:
- `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` after reordering, adding and removing nodes, for flat trees (level accessor, and children accessor with expand and collapse) and nested trees (children accessor and level accessor).
- A test that counts `expansionKey` calls during one change detection pass of a tree with 200 sibling nodes. It's 20,900 calls before this change and 800 after. The test asserts fewer than 4,000, so it doesn't depend on timing.

Fixes #34163.

### Testing

Bazel can't run the tests natively on Windows (analysis fails because `rules_sass` has no Windows toolchain), so I ran the specs a different way: bundled them in JIT mode with esbuild, using `test/angular-test.init.ts` (zoneless, exhaustive `checkNoChanges`), and ran them with Jasmine in headless Chrome.
- `src/cdk/tree` (all 3 spec files): 113 passed with this change. Without the change to `tree.ts`, only the new call-counting test fails (`Expected 20900 to be less than 4000`).
- `src/material/tree` (all 4 spec files, including the harness): 64 passed.
- `tsc` on the changed files, plus `prettier --check` and `tslint` on them: clean.

CI will be the first run through the repo's Bazel and Web Test Runner setup.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code).

Issues.Title: bug(mat-slider and mat-progress-bar): tracks do not meet contrast requirements
Issues.Body:
### Description

The track has less than 3:1 contrast with the surface behind it (about 1.3:1 for `--mat-sys-secondary-container` on white), so users with low vision can't see how much progress is left. This fails WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.4.11 (Non-text Contrast), and Material Design 3 requires a stop indicator in that case.

Angular Material has no stop indicator and no token for it.

### Reproduction

https://material.angular.dev/components/progress-bar/overview
https://material.angular.dev/components/slider/overview

### Expected Behavior

Slider and Progress Bar are fully accessible and able to meet WCAG 2.2 AA requirements, for example by using a stop indicator on the end of the track.

### Actual Behavior

Slider and Progress Bar are not fully accessible and are unable to meet WCAG 2.2 AA requirements by any supported means.

### Environment

- Angular: v22
- CDK/Material: v22
- Browser(s): any
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): any
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "bug(mat-slider and mat-progress-bar): tracks do not meet contrast requirements" (#34162)

Issues.Title: fix(material/icon): escape the path prefixed to FuncIRI references
Issues.Body:
Escapes backslashes and single quotes in the path (and in the id) before they are interpolated into the `url('…')` value in `_prependPathToReferences`, so a path containing a literal quote cannot terminate the string and add further URL tokens to the attribute. The leading-slash normalization added in #33812 is unchanged, and a path with no `'` or `\` produces exactly the same value as before.

Verified against Chrome's CSS parser: today's value parses as two `url()` tokens when the path contains a quote (the second one resolving to another origin); with this change it parses as a single token on the current origin.

Adds two regression tests next to the existing FuncIRI tests, covering a quote breakout and a backslash + quote path. Both assert that stripping the escape sequences leaves a single quoted URL, which fails on the current code and passes with this change.

Fixes #34159
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(material/icon): escape the path prefixed to FuncIRI references" (#34160)

Issues.Title: bug(material/icon): FuncIRI references can be broken out of the quoted url() string
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

`MatIcon._prependPathToReferences()` interpolates `location.pathname + location.search` into a single-quoted CSS `url('…')` value:

```ts
element.setAttribute(attr.name, `url('${normalizedPath}#${attr.value}')`);
```

A literal `'` is preserved in an HTTP(S) pathname, so a path containing one closes that string early and the remainder of the path is parsed as further CSS tokens in the attribute. `mask` and `filter` accept a list of references, so those extra tokens become additional references rather than being ignored, and one of them can resolve to another origin.

#33812 made the value root-relative for paths beginning with `//`. It does not escape the value, so this case is not covered by it.

### Reproduction

A StackBlitz reproduction is not possible for this one: the input is `location.pathname`, and the StackBlitz preview host does not allow serving the app under an arbitrary path containing a `'`. Minimal local reproduction instead:

1. `ng new demo && cd demo && npm i @angular/material @angular/cdk`
2. Register an icon that uses a `mask` reference and render it with `<mat-icon svgIcon="cover"></mat-icon>`:

```ts
registry.addSvgIconLiteral('cover', sanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml(
  '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="48" height="48">' +
  '<defs><mask id="cover"><circle cx="24" cy="24" r="24" fill="white"/></mask></defs>' +
  '<rect width="48" height="48" fill="#1a73e8" mask="url(#cover)"/></svg>'));
```

3. Build it and serve `index.html` for any request path (a standard SPA history fallback).
4. Open the app at `/safe'),url('https://other.example/x`
5. Inspect the rendered `rect`'s `mask` attribute.

The parsing half can also be seen without an app, which is what makes the impact concrete. In Chrome:

```js
const el = document.createElement('div');
el.style.maskImage = `url('/safe'),url('https://other.example/x#cover')`;
el.style.maskImage;
// => url("/safe"), url("https://other.example/x#cover")   — two references
```

With the quote escaped, the same value parses as a single reference on the current origin.

### Expected Behavior

The rewritten attribute always contains exactly one reference, resolving to the current origin, whatever characters the current path happens to contain.

### Actual Behavior

The attribute can contain more than one reference. With the path above, the rendered `mask` becomes:

```
url('/safe'),url('https://other.example/x#cover')
```

which Chrome parses as two references, the second one pointing at another origin. With a quote-free path the attribute is unchanged, so only paths containing `'` (or `\`) are affected.

### Environment

Angular: 22.x
@angular/cdk, @angular/material: 22.2.2 (the same code is present on `main`)
Browser: Chrome (current)
Node: 22.x
OS: any

Issues.Body:
